sentences.zh: 弭德超 侯莫陳利用 趙贊 王黼 朱勔 王繼先 曾覿龍大淵 附 張說 王抃 姜特立譙熙載 附

translations.literal: Mi Dezhao, Houmochen Liyong, Zhao Zan, Wang Fu, Zhu Mian, Wang Jixian, Zeng Di and Long Dayuan (appendix), Zhang Yue, Wang Bian, Jiang Teli and Qiao Xizai (appendix).
translations.idiomatic: Mi Dezhao; Houmochen Liyong; Zhao Zan; Wang Fu; Zhu Mian; Wang Jixian; Zeng Di and Long Dayuan (supplementary); Zhang Yue; Wang Bian; Jiang Teli and Qiao Xizai (supplementary).

sentences.zh: 人君生長深宮之中，法家、拂士接耳目之時少，宦官、女子共啟處之日多，二者，佞幸之梯媒也。

translations.literal: When a ruler grows up deep within the palace, he has little time when legalists and corrective ministers reach his eyes and ears, but many days when eunuchs and women share his dwelling—these two are the ladder and medium for flatterers and favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in the seclusion of the inner palace, a sovereign hears little from men of law and rectitude, and spends far more of his days in the company of eunuchs and palace women. Both are the very rungs by which flatterers climb into favor.

sentences.zh: 剛明之主亦有佞幸焉，剛好專任，明好偏察，彼佞幸者一投其機，為患深矣。

translations.literal: Even firm and clear-sighted rulers also have flatterers and favorites: the firm-minded tend to entrust power exclusively to one man, the clear-sighted tend toward partial, excessive scrutiny—once those flatterers strike their opening, the harm runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: Even resolute and perceptive emperors are not immune. Strength of will invites exclusive trust; keen sight invites obsessive suspicion—and the moment a sycophant finds his angle, the damage can be profound.

sentences.zh: 他日敗闕，雖能殄除，隳城以求狐，灌社以索鼠，亦曰殆哉！

translations.literal: When failure and faults come later, even if they can be wiped out, it is like destroying the city to catch a fox or flooding the shrine mound to catch a mouse—one may say how perilous!
translations.idiomatic: When the reckoning finally comes, the evil may still be uprooted—but only at the cost of razing a city to catch a fox, or drowning a shrine to flush out a rat. The cure itself is perilous.

sentences.zh: 宋世中材之君，朝有佞幸，所不免也。

translations.literal: Among the Song emperors of middling talent, having flatterers and favorites at court was unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, emperors of merely average ability could scarcely keep flatterers from their courts.

sentences.zh: 太宗有弭德超，趙贊，孝宗有曾覿、龍大淵，二君固不可謂非剛明之主也。

translations.literal: Taizong had Mi Dezhao and Zhao Zan; Xiaozong had Zeng Di and Long Dayuan—these two rulers certainly cannot be said not to have been firm and clear-sighted sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had Mi Dezhao and Zhao Zan; Xiaozong had Zeng Di and Long Dayuan—yet neither can fairly be called a weak or dull-witted ruler.

sentences.zh: 作《佞幸傳》。

translations.literal: [The History] compiled the 'Biographies of Flatterers and Favorites.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence this 'Biographies of Flatterers and Favorites.'

sentences.zh: 弭德超

translations.literal: Mi Dezhao
translations.idiomatic: Mi Dezhao

sentences.zh: 初，太宗念邊戍勞苦，月賜士卒銀，謂之月頭銀。

translations.literal: At first, Taizong, mindful of the hardships of frontier garrison duty, monthly bestowed silver upon the soldiers, calling it 'month-head silver.'
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Taizong, taking pity on the toil of the border garrisons, granted the troops a monthly allowance in silver—known as 'month-head silver.'

sentences.zh: 德超乘間以急變聞于太宗曰：「樞密使曹彬秉政歲久，得士眾心；

translations.literal: Dezhao seized an interval to report an urgent change to Taizong, saying: 'Privy Councillor Cao Bin has held power for many years and has won the hearts of officers and men;
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao seized his chance and urgently reported to Taizong: 'Privy Councillor Cao Bin has held power for years and holds the loyalty of the army;

sentences.zh: 臣從塞上來，聞士卒言：'月頭銀曹公所致，微曹公我輩餒死矣。

translations.literal: I have come from the frontier passes, and I heard the soldiers say: "The month-head silver is owed to Lord Cao; without Lord Cao we would have starved to death."
translations.idiomatic: I have just come from the frontier, and the men say: "Our month-head silver comes from Lord Cao—without him we would have starved."

sentences.zh: '」又巧誣彬他事。

translations.literal: ' He also craftily slandered Bin on other matters.
translations.idiomatic: He also wove other false charges against Bin.

sentences.zh: 上頗疑之，出彬為天平軍節度。

translations.literal: The emperor became quite suspicious and transferred Bin out to serve as military commissioner of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and removed Bin, posting him as military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 以王顯為宣徽南院使，德超為宣徽北院使，並兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: Wang Xian was made Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Attendant Service, and Dezhao Commissioner of the Northern Bureau, both concurrently serving as vice commissioners of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Attendant Service, and Dezhao Commissioner of the Northern Bureau; both were also made vice commissioners of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 德超譖曹彬事成，期得樞密使，乃為副使；

translations.literal: After Dezhao's slander of Cao Bin succeeded, he expected to obtain the post of Privy Councillor, but was only made vice commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Once his plot against Cao Bin had succeeded, Dezhao expected the Privy Councillorship—but received only the vice commissioner's post instead;

sentences.zh: 又柴禹錫與德超官同，先授，班在其上。

translations.literal: moreover, Chai Yuxi held the same rank as Dezhao but had been appointed first, so his precedence was above Dezhao's.
translations.idiomatic: and Chai Yuxi, who held the same rank but had been appointed earlier, outranked him in precedence.

sentences.zh: 故德超視事月餘，稱病請告，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Therefore Dezhao, after holding office for a little over a month, claimed illness and requested leave, always discontented in daily life.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month in office, Dezhao pleaded illness and took leave, brooding in perpetual discontent.

sentences.zh: 一日詬顯及禹錫曰：「我言國家大事，有安社稷功，止得線許大官。

translations.literal: One day he reviled Xian and Yuxi, saying: 'When I speak on great affairs of state and have achievements in securing the altars of state, I receive only this tiny rank.
translations.idiomatic: One day he berated Xian and Yuxi: 'I counsel the throne on matters of state and have done service worthy of the realm—and for it I receive this paltry rank.

sentences.zh: 汝等何人，反在我上，更令我效汝輩所為，我實恥之。」

translations.literal: Who are you people to be above me? To make me imitate what you people do—I am truly ashamed of it.'
translations.idiomatic: Who are you to stand above me? That I should be made to ape your ways—I am ashamed of it.

sentences.zh: 又大罵曰：「：汝輩當斷頭，我度上無守執，為汝輩所眩惑。」

translations.literal: He also cursed violently: 'You people ought to be beheaded! I reckon the emperor has no fixed steadfastness and is deluded by you people.'
translations.idiomatic: He went on to rage: 'You deserve to lose your heads! The emperor has no firm resolve—he is bewitched by the likes of you.'

sentences.zh: 顯告之，太宗怒，命膳部郎中、知雜滕中正就第鞫德超，具伏，下詔奪官職，與其家配隸瓊州禁錮，未幾死。

translations.literal: Xian reported this; Taizong was furious and ordered Teng Zhongzheng, Director of the Palace Catering Office and acting director of miscellaneous affairs, to go to Dezhao's residence to interrogate him. Dezhao fully confessed. An edict stripped him of office, and he and his family were sentenced to penal registration and confinement in Qiong Prefecture. Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xian reported the outburst. Taizong flew into a rage and sent Teng Zhongzheng, Director of the Palace Catering Office and acting miscellaneous-affairs director, to Dezhao's house to examine him. Dezhao confessed everything. Stripped of rank by edict, he and his household were banished to penal service and confined in Qiong Prefecture. He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳利用

translations.literal: Houmochen Liyong
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Liyong

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳利用，益州成都人，幼得變幻之術。

translations.literal: Houmochen Liyong was a native of Chengdu in Yizhou. From childhood he mastered the arts of transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Liyong was a native of Chengdu in Yizhou. From boyhood he mastered the arts of illusion and transformation.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，賣藥京師，言黃白事以惑人。

translations.literal: In the early Taiping Xingguo era, he sold medicine in the capital and spoke of yellow-and-white matters to mislead people.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taiping Xingguo reign he peddled medicines in the capital, preaching the secrets of alchemical gold and silver to beguile the crowd.

sentences.zh: 樞密承旨陳從信白于太宗，即日召見，試其術頗驗，即授殿直，累遷崇儀副使。

translations.literal: Privy Council recipient Chen Congxin reported him to Taizong; that very day he was summoned and tested—his arts proved quite effective—whereupon he was appointed Palace Attendant, and eventually rose to Vice Commissioner of the Commission for Ceremonial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Congxin, recipient at the Privy Council, brought him to Taizong's attention. Summoned that same day and put to the test, his tricks proved convincing; he was appointed Palace Attendant and eventually rose to Vice Commissioner of the Commission for Ceremonial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，改右監門衛將軍，領應州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, he was changed to General of the Right Gate Guard and concurrently made Prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was transferred to General of the Right Gate Guard and given concurrent appointment as Prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，諸將北征，以利用與王侁並為并州駐泊都監，擢單州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year, as the various generals marched north, Liyong and Wang Huo were together made garrison commissioners stationed at Bingzhou, and he was promoted to Prefect of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the generals marched north, Liyong and Wang Huo were jointly made garrison commissioners at Bingzhou, and Liyong was promoted to Prefect of Shan.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷鄭州團練使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Regimentation Commissioner of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Regimentation Commissioner of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 前後賜與甚渥，依附者頗獲進用，遂橫恣無復畏憚。

translations.literal: Before and after, his gifts and favors were exceedingly generous; those who attached themselves to him often gained advancement, and so he grew arrogant and unrestrained, no longer fearing or restraining himself.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial largesse flowed to him in abundance, and those who clung to his coattails often won promotion. Emboldened, he grew insolent and unchecked, fearing nothing and no one.

sentences.zh: 其居處服玩皆僭乘輿，人畏之不敢言。

translations.literal: His dwelling, clothing, and ornaments all usurped imperial prerogatives; people feared him and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: His residence, dress, and furnishings all trespassed on imperial privilege. Men feared him and held their tongues.

sentences.zh: 會趙普再入中書，廉知殺人及諸不法，盡奏之。

translations.literal: When Zhao Pu reentered the Central Secretariat, he personally uncovered murders and various illegal acts and memorialized all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pu returned to the Central Secretariat, he personally investigated murders and a host of other crimes and memorialized the full record to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣近臣案得奸狀，欲貸其死，普固請曰：「陛下不誅，是亂天下法。

translations.literal: Taizong dispatched a close attendant to investigate and confirm the criminal evidence; he wished to spare his life, but Pu firmly petitioned: 'If Your Majesty does not execute him, you will be throwing the laws of the realm into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent a trusted attendant to verify the charges and wished to spare Liyong's life, but Pu pressed him hard: 'If Your Majesty does not put this man to death, you will overturn the law of the land.

sentences.zh: 法可惜，此何足惜哉！」

translations.literal: The law is worth sparing—this man is not worth sparing!'
translations.idiomatic: The law is worth preserving—this man is not!'

sentences.zh: 遂下詔除名，配商州禁錮。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued stripping his name from the rolls, and he was sentenced to penal registration and confinement in Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed stripping his name from the registers and sentencing him to penal registration and confinement in Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初籍其家，俄詔還之。

translations.literal: Initially his household property was confiscated and registered; shortly thereafter an edict returned it.
translations.idiomatic: At first his property was confiscated and inventoried; soon afterward an edict ordered it restored.

sentences.zh: 趙普恐其復用，因殿中丞竇諲嘗監鄭州榷酤，知利用每獨南向坐以接京使，犀玉帶用紅黃羅袋；

translations.literal: Zhao Pu, fearing he would be restored to office, took advantage of the fact that Palace Director Dou Yin had once supervised the wine monopoly at Zheng Prefecture and knew that Liyong always sat alone facing south to receive capital envoys, and used a rhinoceros-horn and jade belt with red and yellow silk pouches;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu, fearing Liyong might be recalled, turned to Palace Director Dou Yin, who had once overseen the wine monopoly at Zheng and knew that Liyong always received capital envoys seated alone facing south, wearing a rhinoceros-horn and jade belt in red and yellow silk pouches—

sentences.zh: 澶州黃河清，鄭州用為詩題試舉人，利用判試官狀，言甚不遜。

translations.literal: when the Yellow River at Chan Prefecture ran clear, Zheng Prefecture used it as a poetic topic to test examination candidates; Liyong, judging the chief examiner's report, spoke with great insolence.
translations.idiomatic: when the Yellow River at Chan ran clear, Zheng Prefecture set it as the theme for a literary examination; Liyong, reviewing the chief examiner's report, wrote with brazen insolence.

sentences.zh: 召諲至中書詰實，令上疏告之。

translations.literal: [Zhao Pu] summoned Yin to the Central Secretariat to verify the facts and ordered him to submit a memorial reporting Liyong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu summoned Yin to the Central Secretariat to confirm the facts and ordered him to submit a memorial denouncing Liyong.

sentences.zh: 又京西轉運副使宋沆籍利用家，得書數紙，言皆指斥切害，悉以進上。

translations.literal: Also, Vice Transport Commissioner Song Hang of the Western Capital circuit registered Liyong's household property and obtained several sheets of writing, all of which contained pointed, cutting, and harmful statements; he presented them all to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Song Hang, Vice Transport Commissioner of the Western Capital circuit, inventoried Liyong's household and found several pages of writing filled with bitter, scathing invective, all of which he forwarded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，令中使臠殺之，已而復遣使貸其死，乘疾置至新安，馬旋濘而踣，出濘換馬，比追及之，已為前使誅矣。

translations.literal: Taizong was enraged and ordered an inner palace envoy to dismember and kill him; then he again sent an envoy to spare his life. [Liyong] was placed on a cart while ill and taken to Xin'an; the horse immediately sank into mud and stumbled—after leaving the mud they changed horses, but by the time they caught up, the previous envoy had already executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's wrath was kindled; he ordered a palace envoy to execute Liyong by dismemberment, then sent another envoy to commute the sentence. Liyong, gravely ill, was carted toward Xin'an; the horse at once foundered in the mire and fell. They changed horses after clearing the mud, but when the second envoy caught up, the first had already carried out the execution.

sentences.zh: 趙贊，并州人，性險詖辯給，好言利害。

translations.literal: Zhao Zan was a native of Bingzhou, treacherous, crafty, quick-tongued, and fond of speaking of advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zan was a native of Bingzhou—treacherous, cunning, glib of tongue, and ever ready to discourse on profit and loss.

sentences.zh: 初為軍小吏，與都校不協，因誣營中謀叛，劉繼元屠之無遺類，稍署贊右職。

translations.literal: Initially a minor military clerk, he did not get along with the garrison commander; he therefore falsely accused the camp of plotting rebellion. Liu Jiyuan slaughtered them without leaving a survivor, and gradually appointed Zan to a higher post.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a lowly military clerk and fell out with the garrison commander. He then falsely denounced the camp for plotting rebellion; Liu Jiyuan massacred every man involved and gradually elevated Zan to more responsible posts.

sentences.zh: 太原平，隸三司為走吏，又許本司補殿直，太宗頗任之。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan was pacified, he was assigned to the Three Departments as a runner-clerk; he also obtained a commission as Palace Attendant through his office; Taizong greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiyuan fell he entered the Three Departments as a runner-clerk, then secured appointment as Palace Attendant through his bureau. Taizong came to rely on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 遷供奉官、閤門祗候，提舉京西、陝西數州錢帛，發摘甚眾。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Service Officer and Envoy Receiving Officer at the Gate, and put in charge of coin and silk in several prefectures of the Western Capital and Shaanxi circuits; his denunciations were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Service Officer and Envoy Receiving Officer at the Gate, he was charged with overseeing coin and silk across several prefectures of the Western Capital and Shaanxi circuits, and his denunciations multiplied.

sentences.zh: 又自乞捕盜，至永興，得兵士盜錢二百，欲磔諸市，知府張齊賢奪而釋之。

translations.literal: He also personally requested to capture robbers; reaching Yongxing, he found a soldier who had stolen two hundred [strings of cash], and wished to dismember him in the marketplace; Prefect Zhang Qixian seized and released him.
translations.idiomatic: He also volunteered to hunt down bandits. At Yongxing he caught a soldier who had stolen two hundred strings of cash and sought to have him torn apart in the marketplace; Prefect Zhang Qixian intervened and set the man free.

sentences.zh: 太宗命御史台按問，停贊官數月。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered the Censorate to investigate; Zan was suspended from office for several months.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered the Censorate to investigate, and Zan was suspended from office for several months.

sentences.zh: 復令專鉤校三司簿，令贊自選吏十數人為耳目，專伺中書、樞密及三司事，乘間白之。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to specialize in auditing the Three Departments ledgers; Zan was allowed to select over ten clerks as eyes and ears to exclusively watch affairs of the Central Secretariat, Privy Council, and Three Departments, reporting them opportunely.
translations.idiomatic: He was then put in charge of auditing the Three Departments ledgers, allowed to handpick a dozen clerks as his eyes and ears to watch the Central Secretariat, the Privy Council, and the Three Departments, and to report whatever he found at the first opportunity.

sentences.zh: 太宗以為忠無他腸，中外益畏其口。

translations.literal: Taizong regarded him as loyal with no ulterior motive; inside and outside court increasingly feared his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong took him for a loyal man without hidden designs, and throughout the court and bureaucracy men grew ever more afraid of his tongue.

sentences.zh: 會改三司官屬，以贊為西京作坊副使、度支都監。

translations.literal: When the Three Departments offices were reformed, Zan was made Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshop and Director of Revenue Expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Departments were reorganized, Zan was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshop and Director of Revenue Expenditure.

sentences.zh: 時又有鄭昌嗣者，宣州人，亦起三司役吏，稍遷侍禁。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Zheng Changsi, a native of Xuan Prefecture, likewise rising from a Three Departments service clerk, gradually promoted to Palace Attendant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Zheng Changsi of Xuan Prefecture, who likewise rose from a menial clerk in the Three Departments and was gradually promoted to Palace Attendant Guard.

sentences.zh: 奉使西川，回奏在官不治者數十人，太宗嘉其直。

translations.literal: Sent on mission to Western Sichuan; on returning he memorialized that several tens of officials were not governing properly, and Emperor Taizong praised his directness.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Western Sichuan, he returned to report that dozens of officials were neglecting their duties, and Emperor Taizong praised his blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 會市物吏因緣為奸，列肆屢謁開封訴之，乃置雜買務，使昌嗣監之。

translations.literal: It happened that purchasing clerks used their positions to commit fraud; shopkeepers repeatedly went to Kaifeng to complain, so the Miscellaneous Purchases Office was established and Changsi was made to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: When purchasing clerks began abusing their posts for private gain, merchants repeatedly petitioned the Kaifeng authorities; the court therefore established the Miscellaneous Purchases Office and put Changsi in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 昌嗣乞著籍便殿門，許非時入奏，與贊親比相表裏，累遷至西上閣門副使、鹽鐵都監。

translations.literal: Changsi requested registration at the Convenient Hall Gate and was permitted to enter and memorialize at irregular times; he and Zan grew close and supported each other inside and out, rising in succession to Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Gateway and Director of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: Changsi asked to be registered at the Convenient Hall Gate and was granted leave to enter and report at any hour. He and Zan drew close, backing each other openly and in secret, and through successive promotions rose to Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Gateway and Director of the Salt and Iron Monopoly.

sentences.zh: 二人既得聯事，由是益橫恣，所為皆不法。

translations.literal: Once the two men were joined in office, from this they became all the more arrogant and reckless, and everything they did was unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two men held office together, they grew still more arrogant and lawless in all they did.

sentences.zh: 太宗頗知之，以問左右，皆畏二人，無敢言其惡。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong knew something of this and questioned those around him, but all feared the two men and none dared speak of their wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had some knowledge of this and questioned those around him, but all feared the two men and none dared speak of their crimes.

sentences.zh: 至道元年上元節，京城張燈，太宗以上清宮成，臨幸。

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival in the first year of Zhidao, lanterns were hung throughout the capital; because the Shangqing Palace had been completed, the emperor visited it in person.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival of the first year of Zhidao, the capital was hung with lanterns; with the Shangqing Palace newly completed, the emperor went in person to visit it.

sentences.zh: 贊與昌嗣邀其黨數人，攜妓樂登宮中玉皇閤，飲宴至夜分；

translations.literal: Zan and Changsi invited several members of their faction, brought singing girls and musicians, and ascended the Jade Emperor Pavilion within the palace, feasting and drinking until late in the night;
translations.idiomatic: Zan and Changsi invited several of their partisans, brought courtesans and musicians, and climbed to the Jade Emperor Pavilion inside the palace, where they feasted and drank deep into the night;

sentences.zh: 掌舍宦者不能止，以其事聞。

translations.literal: The palace attendants in charge of lodging could not stop them and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendants charged with keeping order could not restrain them and reported what had happened.

sentences.zh: 太宗大怒，並摭諸事，下詔奪贊官，許攜家配隸房州禁錮，即日驛遣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was greatly enraged; gathering up their various offenses, he issued an edict stripping Zan of office, permitting him to take his family into exile as registered bondsmen under house arrest in Fangzhou, and had him dispatched the same day by post.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was furious. Collecting their various offenses, he issued an edict stripping Zan of rank, allowing him to take his family into exile as registered bondsmen under house arrest in Fangzhou, and had him sent off that same day by courier.

sentences.zh: 昌嗣黜唐州團練副使，不署事。

translations.literal: Changsi was demoted to Deputy Military Training Commissioner of Tangzhou, without assigned duties.
translations.idiomatic: Changsi was demoted to Deputy Military Training Commissioner of Tangzhou, a post without actual responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 既數日，並賜死于路。

translations.literal: After several days, both were granted death on the road.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, both were ordered to take their own lives on the road.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂侍臣曰：「君子小人如芝蘭荊棘，不能絕其類，在人甄別耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to his attendant ministers: "The gentleman and the petty man are like orchids and thorns — one cannot extinguish their kinds; it rests with men to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said to his ministers: "The gentleman and the petty man are like orchids and thorns. One cannot wipe out either kind; it is for men to tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 苟盡君子，則何用刑罰焉？」

translations.literal: If all were gentlemen, of what use would punishments be?"
translations.idiomatic: If everyone were a gentleman, what need would there be for punishments?"

sentences.zh: 參知政事寇准對曰：「帝堯之時，四凶在庭，則三代之前，世質民淳，已有小人矣。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Kou Zhun replied: "In the time of Emperor Yao, the Four Criminals were in court — so even before the Three Dynasties, when the age was simple and the people pure, petty men already existed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Kou Zhun replied: "Even in the age of Emperor Yao the Four Criminals sat in court—so before the Three Dynasties, in that plain and unsophisticated age, petty men already existed.

sentences.zh: 今之衣儒服、居清列者，亦頗朋附小人，為自安計。

translations.literal: Those today who wear Confucian robes and occupy high offices also rather frequently attach themselves to petty men, for the sake of their own security.
translations.idiomatic: Those who today wear Confucian robes and hold high office also often attach themselves to petty men for their own safety.

sentences.zh: 如贊、昌嗣之類奔走賤吏，不足言也。」

translations.literal: Men like Zan and Changsi, scurrying petty clerks, are not worth mentioning."
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zan and Changsi—scurrying petty clerks—are hardly worth speaking of."

sentences.zh: 王黼字將明，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Wang Fu, courtesy name Jiangming, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu, courtesy name Jiangming, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初名甫，後以同東漢宦官，賜名黼。

translations.literal: His original given name was Fu; later, because it was the same as that of an Eastern Han eunuch, he was granted the name Fu.
translations.idiomatic: His original given name was Fu; later, because it matched that of an Eastern Han eunuch, the throne granted him the name Fu.

sentences.zh: 為人美風姿，目睛如金，有口辯，才疏雋而寡學術，然多智善佞。

translations.literal: In person he had a fine bearing, eyes bright as gold; he was glib of tongue, clever and quick-witted but lacking in learning, yet cunning and skilled at flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing, with eyes bright as gold, he was quick of tongue—clever and sharp-witted, though shallow in learning—yet full of wiles and skilled at flattery.

sentences.zh: 中崇甯進士第，調相州司理參軍，編修《九域圖志》，何志同領局，喜其人，為父執中言之，薦擢校書郎，遷符寶郎、左司諫。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the Chongning era, was appointed judicial administrator of Xiangzhou, and helped compile the Gazetteer of the Nine Regions; He Zhitong headed the bureau, took a liking to him, spoke of him to his father Zhizhong, and had him recommended and promoted to proofreader, then transferred to seal keeper and Left Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the Chongning era and was appointed judicial administrator of Xiangzhou. While compiling the Gazetteer of the Nine Regions under He Zhitong, he won He's favor; He spoke of him to his father Zhizhong, who recommended him for promotion to proofreader, and he was later transferred to seal keeper and Left Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 張商英在相位，浸失帝意，遣使以玉環賜蔡京于杭；

translations.literal: When Zhang Shangying was chief councillor he gradually lost the emperor's favor; he sent an envoy to bestow a jade ring on Cai Jing at Hangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang Shangying held the chancellorship he gradually lost the emperor's favor and sent an envoy to Hangzhou to bestow a jade ring on Cai Jing;

sentences.zh: 黼覘知之，數條奏京所行政事，並擊商英。

translations.literal: Fu learned of this by secret observation and repeatedly submitted detailed memorials on policies Cai Jing was carrying out, attacking Shangying as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fu discovered this through secret observation and repeatedly submitted detailed memorials on Cai Jing's policies, attacking Shangying as well.

sentences.zh: 京復相，德其助己，除左諫議大夫、給事中、御史中丞，自校書至是財兩歲。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing returned to the chancellorship, grateful for his help, he appointed Fu Left Grand Master of Remonstrance, Attendant Censor, and Vice Censor-in-Chief — from proofreader to this in only two years.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing returned to power, grateful for his assistance, he appointed Fu Left Grand Master of Remonstrance, Attendant Censor, and Vice Censor-in-Chief—from proofreader to these posts in only two years.

sentences.zh: 黼因執中進，乃欲去執中，使京顓國，遂疏其二十罪，不聽。

translations.literal: Fu had risen through Zhizhong's patronage, but now wished to remove Zhizhong so that Cai Jing might monopolize state power; he therefore memorialized twenty charges against him, but the court did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had risen through Zhizhong's patronage, but now wished to remove him so that Cai Jing could monopolize the government; he therefore submitted a memorial listing twenty crimes against Zhizhong, but the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 俄兼侍讀，進翰林學士。

translations.literal: Shortly he was also made Lecturer-in-Attendance and promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also made Lecturer-in-Attendance and promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 京與鄭居中不合，黼復內交居中，京怒，徙為戶部尚書，大農方乏，將以邦用不給為之罪。

translations.literal: Cai Jing was at odds with Zheng Juzhong; Fu again cultivated a secret alliance with Juzhong. Cai Jing was angry and transferred him to Minister of Revenue — the state granaries were then depleted, and Cai intended to charge him with the state's finances being insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing fell out with Zheng Juzhong, and Fu secretly allied himself with Juzhong again. Cai Jing was enraged and transferred him to Minister of Revenue; the state granaries were then empty, and Cai intended to blame him for the treasury's shortfall.

sentences.zh: 既而諸班禁旅賚犒不如期，詣左藏鼓噪，黼聞之，即諸軍揭大榜，期以某月某日，眾讀榜皆散，京計不行。

translations.literal: Before long the various units of the imperial guard, finding their reward stipends had not arrived on time, went to the Left Treasury and raised a clamor. When Fu heard of this, he immediately had notices posted in each army unit fixing a date in such-and-such month and day; the men read the notices and all dispersed — Cai Jing's plan failed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the various units of the imperial guard, finding their reward stipends overdue, went to the Left Treasury and raised an uproar. When Fu heard of it, he immediately had large notices posted in every camp promising payment on a fixed date; the men read the notices and dispersed, and Cai Jing's scheme came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 還為學士，進承旨。

translations.literal: He was restored as Academician and promoted to Academician-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to Hanlin Academician and promoted to Academician-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 蔡京致仕，黼陽順人心，悉反其所為，罷方田，毀辟雍、醫、算學，並會要、六典諸局，汰省吏，減遙郡使、橫班官奉入之半，茶鹽鈔法不復比較，富戶科抑一切蠲除之，四方翕然稱賢相。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing retired, Fu outwardly followed the people's wishes and wholly reversed what Cai had done: he abolished the equal-field system, dismantled the Imperial Academy and the medical and arithmetic schools, merged the offices for state compilations including the Comprehensive Statutes and the Six Canons, cut redundant clerks, halved the salaries of commissioners in distant prefectures and horizontal-rank officials, ceased audits under the tea-and-salt certificate system, and completely remitted all surcharges on wealthy households — and everywhere people suddenly hailed him as a worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing retired, Fu outwardly followed popular sentiment and reversed nearly everything Cai had done: he abolished the equal-field system, dismantled the Imperial Academy and the medical and arithmetic schools, merged the offices compiling the Comprehensive Statutes, the Six Canons, and other state works, cut redundant clerks, halved the salaries of commissioners in distant prefectures and horizontal-rank officials, stopped audits under the tea-and-salt certificate system, and remitted all surcharges levied on wealthy households. Everywhere people suddenly hailed him as a worthy chancellor.

sentences.zh: 既得位，乘高為邪，多畜子女玉帛自奉，僭擬禁省。

translations.literal: Once he had secured his position, he rode his elevation to do evil, hoarding women, jade, and silk for his own pleasure, presumptuously imitating the inner palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Once secure in power, he abused his high station for wicked ends, hoarding women, jade, and silk for his own indulgence and presumptuously copying the style of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 誘奪徽猷閣待制鄧之綱妾，反以罪竄之綱嶺南。

translations.literal: He seduced and seized the concubine of Deng Zhigang, Attendant Drafting Official of the Huiyao Pavilion, and instead charged Deng with a crime and banished him to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He seduced and seized the concubine of Deng Zhigang, Attendant Drafting Official of the Huiyao Pavilion, then turned about, charged Deng with a crime, and banished him to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 加少保、太宰。

translations.literal: He was given the additional titles Junior Tutor and Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional titles of Junior Tutor and Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 請置應奉局，自兼提領，中外名錢皆許擅用，竭天下財力以供費。

translations.literal: He requested the establishment of a Tribute Service Bureau, taking its direct supervision upon himself; all named funds internal and external to the court were permitted for his arbitrary use, draining the empire's wealth to supply his expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: He requested the creation of a Tribute Service Bureau and put himself in charge of it; every named fund inside and outside the court was placed at his disposal, and he drained the empire's wealth to supply his expenses.

sentences.zh: 官吏承望風旨，凡四方水土珍異之物，悉苛取於民，進帝所者不能什一，餘皆入其家。

translations.literal: Officials, seeking to comply with his intent, everywhere harshly extracted from the people every rare thing of local land and water; what reached the emperor's palace did not amount to one tenth — the rest all entered his household.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, eager to follow his wishes, harshly extorted from the people every rare product of land and water from every region; what reached the emperor amounted to less than one tenth, and the rest went into Fu's own house.

sentences.zh: 御史陳過庭乞盡罷以御前使喚為名冗官，京西轉運使張汝霖請罷進西路花果，帝既納，黼復露章劾之，兩人皆徙遠郡。

translations.literal: The censor Chen Guoting petitioned to abolish entirely the superfluous offices called 'imperial summons attendants'; the Transport Commissioner of Jingxi, Zhang Rulin, petitioned to end the western-route tribute of fruits and flowers. After the emperor had accepted these proposals, Fu submitted an open memorial impeaching them both, and the two men were both transferred to distant prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Guoting petitioned to abolish entirely the superfluous offices known as imperial summons attendants; Jingxi Transport Commissioner Zhang Rulin asked to end the western-route tribute of fruits and flowers. After the emperor accepted these proposals, Fu submitted an open impeachment against them both, and the two men were transferred to distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 睦寇方臘起，黼方文太平，不以告，蔓延彌月，遂攻破六郡。

translations.literal: The bandit Fang La rose in rebellion in Mu; Fu was then composing essays celebrating peace and did not report it — it spread for more than a month, until six prefectures were broken and overrun.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Fang La rose in Mu Prefecture, but Fu was then composing essays celebrating peace and did not report it; the rebellion spread for more than a month until six prefectures had been overrun.

sentences.zh: 帝遣童貫督秦甲十萬始平之。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Tong Guan to command one hundred thousand Qin-region troops before the rebellion was finally suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Tong Guan to command one hundred thousand troops from the Qin region before the rebellion was finally put down.

sentences.zh: 猶以功轉少傅，又進少師。

translations.literal: Fu was nonetheless transferred to Junior Preceptor for this merit, and later promoted to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was nonetheless promoted to Junior Preceptor for this achievement, and later advanced to Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 貫之行也，帝全付以東南一事，謂之曰：「如有急，即以御筆行之。」

translations.literal: When Tong set out, the emperor wholly entrusted him with affairs in the southeast, saying to him: "If there is urgency, act by imperial brush alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong set out, the emperor wholly entrusted him with affairs in the southeast and said to him: "If there is urgency, act on the authority of the imperial brush alone.

sentences.zh: 貫至吳，見民困花石之擾，眾言：「賊不亟平，坐此耳。」

translations.literal: When Tong reached Wu, he saw the people harried by the Huashi tribute, and many said: "If the rebels are not quickly suppressed, it is on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong reached Wu, he saw the people worn down by the Huashi tribute, and many said: "If the rebels are not quickly crushed, it is because of this.

sentences.zh: 貫即命其僚董耘作手詔，若罪已然，且有罷應奉局之令，吳民大悅。

translations.literal: Tong at once had his aide Dong Yun draft a handwritten edict, as if the fault were already acknowledged, and including an order to abolish the Tribute Service Bureau — the people of Wu were greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Tong at once had his aide Dong Yun draft a handwritten edict, as though guilt had already been confessed and including an order to abolish the Tribute Service Bureau; the people of Wu were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 貫平賊歸，黼言於帝曰：「臘之起由茶鹽法也，而貫入奸言，歸過陛下。」

translations.literal: After Tong suppressed the rebels and returned, Fu said to the emperor: "La's rising was due to the tea-and-salt laws, yet Tong has taken in malicious counsel and shifted the blame onto Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: After Tong suppressed the rebels and returned, Fu said to the emperor: "La's rebellion arose from the tea-and-salt laws, yet Tong has taken in malicious counsel and shifted the blame onto Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 帝怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged.

sentences.zh: 貫謀起蔡京以間黼，黼懼。

translations.literal: Tong plotted to bring Cai Jing back to drive a wedge against Fu, and Fu was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Tong plotted to restore Cai Jing in order to drive a wedge against Fu, and Fu grew afraid.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷已納趙良嗣之計，結女真共圖燕，大臣多不以為可。

translations.literal: At this time the court had already adopted Zhao Liangsi's plan to ally with the Jurchen and jointly seize Yan; most senior ministers did not consider it advisable.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court had already adopted Zhao Liangsi's plan to ally with the Jurchen and jointly seize Yan, though most senior ministers did not think it wise.

sentences.zh: 黼曰：「南北雖通好百年，然自累朝以來，彼之慢我者多矣。

translations.literal: Fu said: "Although North and South have been at peace for a hundred years, from successive reigns onward they have often slighted us.
translations.idiomatic: Fu said: "Although North and South have been at peace for a hundred years, from reign after reign they have often treated us with contempt.

sentences.zh: 兼弱攻昧，武之善經也。

translations.literal: To combine with the weak and attack the obtuse — that is the supreme principle of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: To ally with the weak and strike the incompetent—that is the highest art of war.

sentences.zh: 今弗取，女真必強，中原故地將不復為我有。」

translations.literal: If we do not seize it now, the Jurchen will surely grow strong, and the old lands of the central plain will no longer be ours.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not take it now, the Jurchen will surely grow strong, and the old lands of the Central Plain will never be ours again.

sentences.zh: 帝雖向其言，然以兵屬貫，命以保民觀釁為上策。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was inclined toward his words, he placed the army under Tong's command and ordered that protecting the people and watching for an opening should be the highest strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor was inclined to agree, he placed the army under Tong's command and ordered that protecting the people and watching for an opening should be the highest strategy.

sentences.zh: 黼復折簡通誠於貫曰：「太師若北行，願盡死力。」

translations.literal: Fu again sent Tong a letter pledging sincerity, saying: "If the Grand Mentor goes north, I wish to exert myself to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Fu then sent Tong a letter pledging his sincerity, saying: "If the Grand Mentor goes north, I shall devote myself to the utmost."

sentences.zh: 時帝方以睦寇故悔其事，及黼一言，遂復治兵。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was just then regretting the affair on account of the Mu rebels; after a single remark from Fu, he again prepared for war.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just begun to regret the whole undertaking because of the Fang La rebellion in Mu, but after a single word from Fu, he resumed military preparations.

sentences.zh: 黼於三省置經撫房，專治邊事，不關之樞密。

translations.literal: Fu established frontier pacification offices in the Three Departments, exclusively to handle border affairs, without involving the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fu set up frontier-pacification offices within the Three Departments to handle border affairs exclusively, bypassing the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 括天下丁夫，計口出算，得錢六千二百萬緡，竟買空城五六而奏凱。

translations.literal: He conscripted laborers throughout the empire, levied a per-capita assessment, and obtained sixty-two million strings of cash; in the end he 'purchased' five or six empty cities and reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: He conscripted laborers empire-wide and levied a head tax, raising sixty-two million strings of cash; he then 'recovered' five or six deserted cities and reported a triumph.

sentences.zh: 率百僚稱賀，帝解玉帶以賜，優進太傅，封楚國公，許服紫花袍，騶從儀物幾與親王等。

translations.literal: He led the hundred officials in offering congratulations; the emperor removed his jade belt and bestowed it on him, graciously promoted him to Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed him as Duke of Chu, permitted him to wear the purple flowered robe, and his ceremonial escorts and insignia nearly matched those of imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: He led the hundred officials in offering congratulations. The emperor removed his own jade belt and bestowed it on him, graciously promoted him to Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed him as Duke of Chu, and permitted him to wear the purple flowered robe; his ceremonial escorts and insignia nearly equaled those of imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 黼議上尊號，帝曰：「此神宗皇帝所不敢受者也。」

translations.literal: Fu proposed an honorific title for the emperor. The emperor said: "This is what Emperor Shenzong himself did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Fu proposed that an honorific title be bestowed upon the emperor. The emperor said, "Even Emperor Shenzong did not dare accept such a thing.

sentences.zh: 卻弗許。

translations.literal: He refused and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 始，遼使至，率迂其驛程，燕犒不示以華侈。

translations.literal: At first, when Liao envoys arrived, their postal routes were usually detoured and delayed, and banquets and rewards at Yan were not displayed with lavish extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Liao envoys arrived, their routes were usually lengthened and their progress delayed; the banquets and rewards at Yan were kept plain, without ostentatious display.

sentences.zh: 及黼務於欲速，令女真使以七日自燕至都，每張宴其居，輒陳尚方錦繡、金玉、瑰寶，以誇富盛，由是女真益生心。

translations.literal: When Fu, eager for speed, ordered Jurchen envoys to travel from Yan to the capital in seven days, at every banquet in their lodging he would display imperial brocades, jades, gold, and rare treasures to boast of wealth and power — and from this the Jurchen grew still more ambitious.
translations.idiomatic: But Fu, impatient for results, ordered Jurchen envoys to reach the capital from Yan in seven days. At every banquet held in their quarters he displayed imperial brocades, jades, gold, and rare treasures to flaunt the empire's wealth — and the Jurchen grew still more covetous.

sentences.zh: 身為三公，位元宰，至陪扈曲宴，親為俳優鄙賤之役，以獻笑取悅。

translations.literal: Though he was one of the Three Dukes and held the chief ministership, at private banquets in the emperor's company he personally performed the vulgar duties of a low actor to win laughter and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Though he ranked among the Three Dukes and held the chief ministership, at the emperor's private banquets he would personally play the buffoon — performing the meanest comic roles to win laughter and favor.

sentences.zh: 欽宗在東宮，惡其所為。

translations.literal: Qinzong, then in the Eastern Palace, detested his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzong, then crown prince, detested his conduct.

sentences.zh: 鄆王楷有寵，黼為陰畫奪宗之策。

translations.literal: Prince Yun Ke enjoyed imperial favor, and Fu secretly devised a plan to seize the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yun Ke enjoyed the emperor's favor, and Fu secretly plotted to supplant the heir.

sentences.zh: 皇孫諶為節度使、崇國公，黼謂但當得觀察使，召宮臣耿南仲諭指，使草代東宮辭諶官奏，竟奪之，蓋欲以是撼搖東宮。

translations.literal: The imperial grandson Shen held the posts of military commissioner and Duke of Chongguo; Fu said he should receive only an observation commissioner. He summoned the palace official Geng Nanzhong, explained his intent, and had him draft a memorial on the crown prince's behalf resigning Shen's offices — and in the end stripped Shen of them, intending thereby to shake the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson Shen held the posts of military commissioner and Duke of Chongguo. Fu declared that he deserved only an observation commissioner, summoned the palace official Geng Nanzhong, explained his intent, and had him draft a memorial on the crown prince's behalf resigning Shen's offices. Shen was stripped of his titles — a move intended to undermine the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝待遇之厚，名其所居閤曰「得賢治定」，為書亭、堂榜九。

translations.literal: The emperor treated him with great favor, naming the hall where he lived "Gaining the Worthy, Order Settled," and personally inscribed nine plaques for his pavilions and halls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him with extraordinary favor, naming his residence hall "Gaining the Worthy, Order Settled," and personally inscribed nine plaques for his pavilions and halls.

sentences.zh: 有玉芝產堂柱，乘輿臨觀之。

translations.literal: When jade-colored fungus sprouted on a hall pillar, the emperor came in person to view it.
translations.idiomatic: When jade-colored fungus sprouted on a hall pillar, the emperor came in person to behold it.

sentences.zh: 梁師成與連牆，穿便門往來，帝始悟其交結狀。

translations.literal: He shared a wall with Liang Shicheng and used a private gate to pass back and forth; the emperor then began to grasp the nature of their collusion.
translations.idiomatic: He shared a wall with Liang Shicheng and used a private gate to pass back and forth; the emperor then began to perceive the full extent of their collusion.

sentences.zh: 還宮，黼眷頓熄，尋命致仕。

translations.literal: After returning to the palace, Fu's favor suddenly cooled; before long he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the palace, imperial favor toward Fu abruptly waned; before long he was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 欽宗受禪，黼惶駭入賀，閤門以上旨不納。

translations.literal: When Qinzong received the abdication, Fu came in panic to offer congratulations, but the Gatekeepers, acting on imperial orders, refused him entry.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong ascended the throne, Fu came in panic to offer congratulations, but the Gatekeepers, acting on imperial orders, refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 金兵入汴，不俟命，載其孥以東。

translations.literal: When the Jin army entered Bian, without awaiting orders he loaded his wife and children and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army entered Bian, he fled east with his family without awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 詔貶為崇信軍節度副使，籍其家。

translations.literal: An edict demoted him to deputy military commissioner of the Chongxin Army and confiscated his household property.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted him to deputy military commissioner of the Chongxin Army and ordered the confiscation of his household property.

sentences.zh: 吳敏、李綱請誅黼，事下開封尹聶山，山方挾宿怨，遣武士躡及于雍丘南輔固村，戕之，民家取其首以獻。

translations.literal: Wu Min and Li Gang requested that Fu be executed; the matter was referred to Kaifeng intendant Nie Shan. Shan, nursing an old grudge, dispatched warriors who tracked Fu to Fugu village south of Yongqiu and killed him; a commoner's household took his head and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Min and Li Gang petitioned for Fu's execution; the case was referred to Kaifeng intendant Nie Shan. Nursing an old grudge, Shan dispatched warriors who tracked Fu to Fugu village south of Yongqiu and killed him. A commoner's household took his head and presented it.

sentences.zh: 帝以初即位，難於誅大臣，托言為盜所殺。

translations.literal: The emperor, having just ascended the throne, found it difficult to execute a great minister and put it about that Fu had been killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having just ascended the throne, was reluctant to execute a great minister and put it about that Fu had been killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 議者不以誅黼為過，而以天討不正為失刑矣。

translations.literal: Commentators did not regard the killing of Fu as a fault, but held that heaven's punishment had not been properly administered — and that this was a failure of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators did not fault the killing of Fu, but held that heaven's judgment had been improperly carried out — a failure of lawful punishment.

sentences.zh: 朱勔，蘇州人。

translations.literal: Zhu Mian was a native of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mian was a native of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父沖，狡獪有智數。

translations.literal: His father Chong was cunning and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong was cunning and full of schemes.

sentences.zh: 家本賤微，庸於人，梗悍不馴，抵罪鞭背。

translations.literal: The family was originally of humble station; he hired himself out as a laborer, was stubborn and unruly, and was punished with a back whipping for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: The family was originally humble; Chong hired himself out as a laborer. Stubborn and unruly, he was punished with a back whipping for an offense.

sentences.zh: 去之旁邑乞貸，遇異人，得金及方書歸，設肆賣藥，病人服之輒效，遠近輻湊，家遂富。

translations.literal: He went to a neighboring county to borrow money, met a strange man, and returned with gold and a book of recipes; he opened a shop selling medicine, and whenever the sick took his remedies they were cured at once — people flocked from near and far, and the family grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: He went to a neighboring county to borrow money, met a strange man, and returned with gold and a book of recipes. He opened a medicine shop, and his remedies cured the sick at once; people flocked from near and far, and the family grew rich.

sentences.zh: 因修蒔園圃，結遊客，致往來稱譽。

translations.literal: He then laid out gardens, cultivated ornamental plants, and befriended traveling guests, winning praise wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out gardens, cultivated ornamental plants, and befriended traveling guests, winning praise wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 始，蔡京居錢塘，過蘇，欲建僧寺閣，會費钜萬，僧言必欲集此緣，非朱沖不可。

translations.literal: At first, when Cai Jing was living at Qiantang and passed through Suzhou, he wished to build a Buddhist temple pavilion; the cost would run to tens of thousands, and the monks said that if this undertaking was to be funded, none but Zhu Chong could do it.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Cai Jing was living at Qiantang and passed through Suzhou, he wished to build a Buddhist temple pavilion at a cost of tens of thousands. The monks said that if the funds were to be raised, none but Zhu Chong could manage it.

sentences.zh: 京以屬郡守，郡守呼沖見京，京語故，沖願獨任。

translations.literal: Cai Jing entrusted the matter to the prefect; the prefect summoned Chong to meet Cai Jing. Cai Jing explained the circumstances, and Chong volunteered to take sole responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing entrusted the matter to the prefect, who summoned Chong to meet him. Cai Jing explained the project, and Chong volunteered to take sole responsibility.

sentences.zh: 居數日，請京詣寺度地，至則大木數千章積庭下，京大驚，陰器其能。

translations.literal: After several days he invited Cai Jing to the temple to survey the site; when Cai Jing arrived, several thousand timbers were piled in the courtyard. Cai Jing was greatly astonished and secretly admired his ability.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he invited Cai Jing to the temple to survey the site. When Cai Jing arrived, several thousand timbers were piled in the courtyard. Cai Jing was astonished and secretly admired his ability.

sentences.zh: 明年召還，挾勔與俱，以其父子姓名屬童貫竄置軍籍中，皆得官。

translations.literal: The next year Cai Jing was recalled to court and brought Mian with him; he had Tong Guan surreptitiously enter the father and son's names in army registers, and both received office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Cai Jing was recalled to court and brought Mian with him. He had Tong Guan surreptitiously enter the father and son's names in army registers, and both received office.

sentences.zh: 徽宗頗垂意花石，京諷勔語其父，密取浙中珍異以進。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong took a keen interest in ornamental flowers and stones; Cai Jing hinted to Mian to tell his father to secretly gather rare treasures from Zhejiang and present them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong took a keen interest in ornamental flowers and stones. Cai Jing hinted to Mian to tell his father to secretly gather rare treasures from Zhejiang and present them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 初致黃楊三本，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: At first he sent three yellow poplar specimens, and the emperor praised them.
translations.idiomatic: At first he sent three yellow poplar specimens, which the emperor praised.

sentences.zh: 後歲歲增加，然歲率不過再三貢，貢物裁五七品。

translations.literal: Later the tribute increased year by year, yet each year there were usually no more than two or three missions, and the items numbered only five or seven kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Later the tribute increased year by year, yet each year there were usually no more than two or three missions, and the items numbered only five or seven kinds.

sentences.zh: 至政和中始極盛，舳艫相銜於淮、汴，號「花石綱」，置應奉局于蘇，指取內帑如囊中物，每取以數十百萬計。

translations.literal: Not until the Zhenghe era did it reach its peak: ships linked stem to stern on the Huai and Bian rivers, in what was called the "Huashi Convoy." A Tribute Service Bureau was established at Suzhou; Mian drew on the inner treasury as though it were money in his own pocket, each time taking tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the Zhenghe era did it reach its peak: ships linked stem to stern on the Huai and Bian rivers in what was called the "Huashi Convoy." A Tribute Service Bureau was established at Suzhou, and Mian drew on the inner treasury as though it were money in his own pocket — each levy running to tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 延福宮、艮岳成，奇卉異植充牣其中。

translations.literal: When the Extended Blessings Palace and Genyue were completed, rare flowers and exotic plants filled them to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Extended Blessings Palace and Genyue were completed, rare flowers and exotic plants filled them to overflowing.

sentences.zh: 勔擢至防禦使，東南部刺史、郡守多出其門。

translations.literal: Mian was promoted to Defense Commissioner, and many prefects and magistrates of the southeast came from his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Mian rose to Defense Commissioner, and many prefects and magistrates of the southeast were his protégés.

sentences.zh: 徐鑄、應安道、王仲閎等濟其惡，竭縣官經常以為奉。

translations.literal: Xu Zhu, Ying Andao, Wang Zhonghong, and others abetted his evil; they drained county regular revenues to supply his tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhu, Ying Andao, Wang Zhonghong, and others abetted his abuses, draining county regular revenues to supply his tribute.

sentences.zh: 所貢物，豪奪漁取於民，毛髮不少償。

translations.literal: The items he presented as tribute were seized from the people by force and plunder, without compensating them so much as a hair.
translations.idiomatic: The tribute items were seized from the people by force and plunder, without compensating them so much as a hair's breadth.

sentences.zh: 士民家一石一木稍堪玩，即領健卒直入其家，用黃封表識，未即取，使護視之，微不謹，即被以大不恭罪。

translations.literal: If in any scholar or commoner's household there was a stone or tree even slightly worth admiring, he would lead strong soldiers straight into the home, mark it with a yellow seal, and though he did not take it immediately, would have it guarded; the slightest lapse in care was punished as the crime of great disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: If any scholar or commoner's household held a stone or tree even slightly worth admiring, he would lead strong soldiers straight into the home and mark it with a yellow seal. Though the item was not taken immediately, guards were posted; the slightest lapse in care was punished as the crime of great disrespect.

sentences.zh: 及發行，必徹屋抉牆以出。

translations.literal: When the time came to transport the goods, they invariably tore down houses and dug through walls to extract them.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came to transport the goods, they invariably tore down houses and dug through walls to extract them.

sentences.zh: 人不幸有一物小異，共指為不祥，唯恐芟夷之不速。

translations.literal: If someone unluckily possessed something even slightly unusual, all would point to it as an ill omen and fear only that it would not be cut down quickly enough.
translations.idiomatic: If someone unluckily possessed something even slightly unusual, neighbors would denounce it as an ill omen and fear only that it would not be uprooted quickly enough.

sentences.zh: 民預是役者，中家悉破產，或鬻賣子女以供其須。

translations.literal: Among the people subject to this corvée, middle households were utterly ruined; some sold their sons and daughters to meet the demands.
translations.idiomatic: Among those subject to this corvée, middle-class households were utterly ruined; some sold their sons and daughters to meet the demands.

sentences.zh: 斫山輦石，程督峭慘，雖在江湖不測之淵，百計取之，必出乃止。

translations.literal: In quarrying mountains and hauling stones, supervision was harsh and cruel; even from the unfathomable depths of lakes and rivers, every method was tried until the stone was extracted — only then would they stop.
translations.idiomatic: In quarrying mountains and hauling stones, supervision was harsh and cruel. Even from the unfathomable depths of lakes and rivers, every method was tried until the stone was extracted — only then would they stop.

sentences.zh: 嘗得太湖石，高四丈，載以巨艦，役夫數千人，所經州縣，有拆水門、橋樑，鑿城垣以過者。

translations.literal: Once he obtained a Tai Lake stone four zhang high, loaded it on a huge ship, and employed several thousand laborers; in the prefectures and counties along the route, water gates and bridges were demolished and city walls breached to let it pass.
translations.idiomatic: Once he obtained a Tai Lake stone four zhang in height, loaded it on a huge ship, and employed several thousand laborers. Along the route, water gates and bridges were demolished and city walls breached to let it pass.

sentences.zh: 既至，賜名「神運昭功石」。

translations.literal: When it arrived, it was given the name "Stone of Divine Transport and Manifest Achievement."
translations.idiomatic: When it arrived, it was given the name "Stone of Divine Transport and Manifest Achievement."

sentences.zh: 截諸道糧餉綱，旁羅商船，揭所貢暴其上，篙工、柁師倚勢貪橫，陵轢州縣，道路相視以目。

translations.literal: He seized grain-transport convoys from every route and roped in merchant ships besides, displaying the tribute openly atop them; the boatmen and helmsmen, relying on their power, were greedy and overbearing, trampling prefectures and counties — travelers on the roads exchanged glances in silence.
translations.idiomatic: He seized grain-transport convoys from every route and requisitioned merchant ships besides, displaying the tribute openly atop them. The boatmen and helmsmen, relying on their power, grew greedy and overbearing, trampling prefectures and counties — travelers on the roads exchanged glances in silent dismay.

sentences.zh: 廣濟卒四指揮盡給挽士猶不足。

translations.literal: All four command units of the Guangji Army were fully assigned as haulers, and still it was not enough.
translations.idiomatic: All four command units of the Guangji Army were fully assigned as haulers, and still it was not enough.

sentences.zh: 京始患之，從容言於帝，願抑其太甚者。

translations.literal: Cai Jing began to worry and gently advised the emperor, expressing a wish to restrain the worst excesses.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing began to worry and gently advised the emperor to restrain the worst excesses.

sentences.zh: 帝亦病其擾，乃禁用糧綱船，戒伐塚藏、毀室廬，毋得加黃封帕蒙人園囿花石，凡十餘事。

translations.literal: The emperor too was troubled by the harassment; he then forbade the use of grain-transport ships, prohibited looting tombs and destroying dwellings, and barred the affixing of yellow-sealed requisitions on people's gardens and ornamental flowers and stones — over ten such measures in all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor too was troubled by the harassment. He forbade the use of grain-transport ships, prohibited looting tombs and destroying dwellings, and barred yellow-sealed requisitions on people's gardens and ornamental flowers and stones — over ten such measures in all.

sentences.zh: 聽勔與蔡攸等六人入貢，餘進奉悉罷。

translations.literal: It was permitted that Mian together with Cai You and five others present tribute; all other submissions were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Only Mian, Cai You, and four others were allowed to send tribute; every other presentation was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 自是勔小戢。

translations.literal: From this Mian slightly restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: After that, Mian pulled back a little.

sentences.zh: 既而勔甚。

translations.literal: Before long Mian became extreme again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was worse than ever.

sentences.zh: 所居直蘇市中孫老橋，忽稱詔，凡橋東西四至壤地室廬悉買賜予己，合數百家，期五日盡徙，郡吏逼逐，民嗟哭于路。

translations.literal: His residence faced Sun Lao Bridge in the Suzhou market; suddenly claiming an edict, all land and dwellings within the four boundaries east and west of the bridge were bought and granted to himself — several hundred households in all; they were given five days to move out entirely; prefectural clerks drove them out, and the people lamented and wept in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: His home stood directly opposite Sun Lao Bridge in the Suzhou market district. Suddenly invoking an imperial order, he had every parcel of land and every dwelling within the bridge's east–west boundaries purchased and deeded to himself—several hundred households in all, given five days to vacate. Prefectural clerks hounded them out, and wailing filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 遂建神霄殿，奉青華帝君像其中，監司、都邑吏朔望皆拜庭下，命士至，輒朝謁，然後通刺詣勔。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built the Divine Empyrean Hall and placed therein an image of the Azure Flower Sovereign Lord; on the new and full moon supervisory commissioners and prefectural and county clerks all bowed in the courtyard; when ordained priests arrived, they first paid court respects, and only then presented calling cards and called on Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He erected a Divine Empyrean Hall and enshrined an image of the Azure Flower Sovereign Lord within it. On the first and fifteenth of each month, supervisory commissioners and local officials bowed in his courtyard. Daoist priests, too, had to pay homage at the hall before they might present their cards and seek an audience with Mian.

sentences.zh: 主趙霖建三十六浦閘，興必不可成之功，天方大寒，役死者相枕藉。

translations.literal: Under his direction Zhao Lin built thirty-six Pu sluice gates, undertaking a project that could not possibly succeed; heaven was at its bitterest cold, and corvée laborers who died lay piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Under his direction Zhao Lin launched construction of thirty-six sluice gates at Pu—an impossible project, launched in the dead of winter. The conscript dead lay stacked like cordwood.

sentences.zh: 霖志在媚勔，益加苛虐，吳、越不勝其苦。

translations.literal: Lin's aim was to ingratiate himself with Mian; he added further harsh cruelty, and Wu and Yue could not bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Lin sought only to please Mian and turned the screws ever tighter; the people of Wu and Yue could endure no more.

sentences.zh: 徽州盧宗原竭庫錢遺之，引為發運使，公肆掊克。

translations.literal: Lu Zongyuan of Huizhou exhaustedly spent treasury funds to give him gifts, had him appointed Transport Commissioner, and he openly and wantonly extorted.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongyuan of Huizhou drained the prefectural treasury showering Mian with gifts and secured him the post of Transport Commissioner—whereupon Mian plundered the region openly and without restraint.

sentences.zh: 園池擬禁籞，服飾器用上僭乘輿。

translations.literal: Gardens and ponds modeled on the imperial enclosure; dress, ornaments, and utensils usurped the imperial carriage regalia.
translations.idiomatic: His gardens and ponds rivaled the imperial park; his dress, furnishings, and ritual objects outstepped what was fit for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又托挽舟募兵數千人，擁以自衛。

translations.literal: He also, under pretext of convoy boat-hauling, recruited several thousand soldiers and surrounded himself with them for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also raised several thousand men under cover of the convoy service and kept them as a private guard.

sentences.zh: 子汝賢等召呼鄉州官寮，頤指目攝，皆奔走聽命，流毒州郡者二十年。

translations.literal: His son Ru Xian and others summoned and called local and prefectural officials; with chin and eye they commanded them, and all ran to obey; they spread poison through prefectures and counties for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ru Xian and the rest summoned officials across town and countryside; a tilt of the chin, a flick of the eye, and men scrambled to obey. Their poison seeped through the southeastern prefectures for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 方臘起，以誅勔為名。

translations.literal: When Fang La rose, he took executing Mian as his rallying cry.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La rebelled, he proclaimed the slaughter of Mian as his cause.

sentences.zh: 童貫出師，承上旨盡罷去花木進奉，帝又黜勔父子弟侄在職者，民大悅。

translations.literal: Tong Guan marched out; carrying out the emperor's intent he entirely abolished flower-and-stone submissions; the emperor also dismissed Mian's sons, brothers, and nephews who held office; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan took the field, he carried out an imperial order to halt all flower-and-stone tribute. The emperor also removed every son, brother, and nephew of Mian's clan who held office. The people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 然寇平，勔復得志，聲焰熏灼。

translations.literal: Yet when the bandits were pacified, Mian again had his way; his renown and power blazed scorchingly.
translations.idiomatic: But once the rebels were suppressed, Mian rose again—and his influence burned hotter than ever.

sentences.zh: 邪人穢夫，候門奴事，自直秘閣至殿學士，如欲可得，不附者旋踵罷去，時謂東南小朝廷。

translations.literal: Wicked men and filthy fellows waited at his gate to serve as slaves; from Attendant of the Secretariat Archive to Hall Academician, whatever one wished could be obtained; those who did not attach themselves were immediately dismissed; people at the time called it the Little Court of the Southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Scoundrels and riffraff thronged his gate like household retainers. Posts from Attendant of the Secretariat Archive to Hall Academician could be had for the asking; anyone who refused to bend was dismissed on the spot. Contemporaries called his domain a petty court of the southeast.

sentences.zh: 帝末年益親任之，居中白事，傳達上旨，大略如內侍，進見不避宮嬪。

translations.literal: In the emperor's later years he grew ever more personally to trust and employ him; from within his residence he reported affairs and conveyed imperial intent—much like an inner eunuch; when entering audience he did not avoid palace women.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor leaned on him ever more heavily. From his own residence Mian reported business and relayed the throne's wishes—much as an inner eunuch might. He entered audience without shying from the palace women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 曆隨州觀察使、慶遠軍承宣使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Suizhou Observation Commissioner and Qingyuan Army Imperial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Suizhou Observation Commissioner and Qingyuan Army Imperial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 燕山奏功，進拜甯遠軍節度使、醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: Reporting merit from the Yanshan campaign, he was promoted and invested as Military Commissioner of the Ningyuan Army and Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Credited with the Yanshan campaign, he was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Ningyuan Army and Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 一門盡為顯官，騶僕亦至金紫，天下為之扼腕。

translations.literal: The whole clan were eminent officials; even outriders and servants reached golden-seal and purple rank; all under heaven clenched their wrists at it.
translations.idiomatic: Every member of his clan held a glittering office; even his grooms and pages wore gold seals and purple robes. The whole empire ground its teeth.

sentences.zh: 靖康之難，欲為自全計，倉卒擁上皇南巡，且欲邀至其第。

translations.literal: At the disaster of Jingkang, seeking a plan for self-preservation, he hastily urged the Retired Emperor on a southern tour, and wished moreover to bring him to his own residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingkang crisis broke, scheming to save himself, he hurriedly pressed the Retired Emperor south on a tour of inspection—and meant to lodge him at his own mansion.

sentences.zh: 欽宗用御史言，放歸田裏，凡由勔得官者皆罷。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong, heeding a censor's advice, sent him back to his fields; all who had obtained office through Mian were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong, acting on a censor's memorial, sent him home to his estates and dismissed everyone who had received office through Mian's patronage.

sentences.zh: 籍其貲財，田至三十萬畝。

translations.literal: His wealth was registered and confiscated; his land reached three hundred thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: His property was seized and inventoried; his land alone totaled three hundred thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 言者不已，羈之衡州，徙韶州、循州，遣使即所至斬之。

translations.literal: Memorialists did not cease; he was detained in Heng Prefecture, transferred to Shao and Xun Prefectures; an envoy was dispatched to behead him wherever he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials kept coming. He was confined in Heng Prefecture, then moved on through Shao and Xun. An imperial agent was sent to execute him on the spot wherever he was found.

sentences.zh: 王繼先

translations.literal: Wang Jixian
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jixian

sentences.zh: 王繼先，開封人。

translations.literal: Wang Jixian was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jixian was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 奸黠善佞。

translations.literal: Treacherous, cunning, and skilled at flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous, quick-witted, and expert at ingratiation.

sentences.zh: 建炎初以醫得幸，其後浸貴寵，世號王醫師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan era he gained favor through medicine; afterward he gradually rose in rank and favor; the world called him Physician Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan reign he won the emperor's favor as a physician. Favor and rank mounted steadily thereafter, and the world knew him as Physician Wang.

sentences.zh: 至和安大夫、開州團練使致仕。

translations.literal: He reached He'an Grand Master and regimental commander of Kaizhou, then retired.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Master for Tranquility and Regimental Commander of Kaizhou, then retired from office.

sentences.zh: 尋以覃恩，改授武功大夫，落致仕。

translations.literal: Soon, through grace of amnesty, he was reassigned as Military Grand Master and his retirement was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: When a general amnesty soon followed, he was reappointed Military Grand Master and recalled from retirement.

sentences.zh: 給事中富直柔奏：「繼先以雜流易前班，則自此轉行無礙，深恐將帥解體。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Fu Zhirou memorialized: "If Jixian exchanges a miscellaneous track for a senior roster post, then henceforth transfers will know no obstruction; I deeply fear the breakdown of generals and commanders."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Fu Zhirou memorialized: "If Jixian trades up from the miscellaneous track into the senior roster, every transfer after this will face no barrier—and I greatly fear the army's commanders will come apart at the seams.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕頃冒海氣，繼先診視有奇效。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I recently suffered from coastal miasma; Jixian's examination and treatment had remarkable effect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I was lately seized by coastal miasma, and Jixian's treatment worked wonders.

sentences.zh: 可特書讀。」

translations.literal: A special decree may be read out."
translations.idiomatic: Issue a special edict and read it aloud.

sentences.zh: 直柔再駁，命乃寢。

translations.literal: Zhirou rebutted again, and the order was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou protested again, and the appointment was shelved.

sentences.zh: 既而特授榮州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long he was specially invested as Defender-in-Chief of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was specially appointed Defender-in-Chief of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太后有疾，繼先診視有勞，特補其子悅道為閣門祗候。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager fell ill, Jixian's diagnosis and treatment earned merit; his son Yuedao was specially appointed Palace Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager fell ill, Jixian tended her with distinction, and his son Yuedao was specially appointed Palace Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋命繼先主管翰林醫官局，力辭。

translations.literal: Soon Jixian was ordered to manage the Hanlin Medical Bureau; he strenuously declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to head the Hanlin Medical Bureau, but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 是時，繼先用事，中外切齒，乃陽乞致仕，以避人言。

translations.literal: At this time Jixian held power; within and without all ground their teeth; he therefore outwardly requested retirement to avoid public talk.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jixian was in power, and hatred for him ran from court to countryside. He pretended to seek retirement to deflect the outcry.

sentences.zh: 詔遷秩二等，許回授。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him two ranks and permitted retroactive conferral.
translations.idiomatic: An edict raised him two ranks and allowed him to confer the benefit on his kin.

sentences.zh: 俄除右武大夫、華州觀察使，詔余人毋得援例。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Right Military Grand Master and Huazhou Observation Commissioner; an edict forbade others to cite his case as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Right Military Grand Master and Huazhou Observation Commissioner, with an edict that no one else might invoke his example.

sentences.zh: 吳貴妃進封，推恩遷奉甯軍承宣使，特封其妻郭氏為郡夫人。

translations.literal: When Consort Wu was advanced in rank, by extended grace he was transferred to Fengning Army Imperial Commissioner; his wife Lady Guo was specially enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Wu received a promotion in rank, Jixian rose with her to Imperial Commissioner of the Fengning Army, and his wife Lady Guo was specially enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 繼先遭遇冠絕人臣，諸大帥承順下風，莫敢少忤，其權勢與秦檜埒。

translations.literal: Jixian's advancement surpassed all ministers; the great commanders yielded and bowed downwind; none dared slightly oppose him; his power matched Qin Hui's.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian's rise outstripped every subject at court. Great field commanders bowed before him; none dared cross him even slightly. His sway matched Qin Hui's.

sentences.zh: 檜使其夫人詣之，敘拜兄弟，表裏引援。

translations.literal: Hui sent his wife to visit him; they exchanged brotherly courtesies; inside and out they mutually patronized.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui sent his wife to call on him; they addressed each other as brothers; openly and behind the scenes they traded favors.

sentences.zh: 遷昭慶軍承宣使，又欲得節鉞，使其徒張孝直等校《本草》以獻，給事中楊椿沮之，計不行。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhaoqing Army Imperial Commissioner, he again wished to obtain a military commission; he had his followers Zhang Xiaozhi and others collate the Materia Medica to present; Supervising Secretary Yang Chun obstructed it, and the plan did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Imperial Commissioner of the Zhaoqing Army, he sought a military commission next and had his followers Zhang Xiaozhi and others revise the Materia Medica as a gift to the throne. Supervising Secretary Yang Chun blocked the move, and the scheme failed.

sentences.zh: 繼先富埒王室，子弟通朝籍，總戎寄，姻戚黨與盤據要途，數十年間，無能搖之者。

translations.literal: Jixian's wealth rivaled the royal house; sons and younger relatives held court registers and military commands; in-laws and cliques occupied critical posts; for several decades none could shake them.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian's fortune rivaled the imperial household. His sons and nephews held court rank and field command; kinsmen and allies clogged the arteries of power. For decades no one could budge them.

sentences.zh: 金兵將至，劉錡請為戰備，繼先乃言：「新進主兵官，好作弗靖，若斬一二人，和好復固。」

translations.literal: When Jin troops were about to arrive, Liu Qi requested war preparations; Jixian then said: "Newly appointed military officials love to stir unrest; if one or two are beheaded, the peace accord will again be firm."
translations.idiomatic: As Jin forces drew near, Liu Qi called for war preparations. Jixian said: "These newly elevated commanders love to stir trouble. Behead one or two of them and the peace will hold firm again.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌曰：「是欲我斬劉錡乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased, said: "Do you want me to behead Liu Qi?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's brow darkened. "Are you asking me to execute Liu Qi?"
