sentences.zh: 侍御史杜莘老劾其十罪，大略謂：「繼先廣造第宅，占民居數百家，都人謂之'快樂仙宮'；

translations.literal: Attending Censor Du Xinlao impeached him on ten crimes, saying in summary: "Jixian broadly built mansions, seizing several hundred households' dwellings; the capital people call it the 'Palace of Joyful Immortals';
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Du Xinlao charged him with ten crimes. In summary: "Jixian has built vast estates, displacing hundreds of families—the people of the capital call his mansion the 'Palace of Joyful Immortals';

sentences.zh: 奪良家婦女為侍妾，鎮江有娼妙於歌舞，矯御前索之；

translations.literal: he seized women from respectable families as concubines; there was a courtesan in Zhenjiang skilled in song and dance—he falsely claimed an imperial requisition for her;
translations.idiomatic: he seized women from respectable families for his harem; when a Zhenjiang courtesan famed for song and dance caught his eye, he forged an order from the palace to claim her;

sentences.zh: 淵聖成喪，舉家燕飲，令妓女舞而不歌，謂之'啞樂'；

translations.literal: when the mourning for the Captive Sage was complete, his whole household feasted; he had courtesans dance but not sing, calling it 'mute music';
translations.idiomatic: when mourning for the Captive Emperor was declared complete, his household gave a banquet and ordered courtesans to dance without singing—calling it 'mute music';

sentences.zh: 自金使來，日輦重寶之吳興，為避走計；

translations.literal: since the Jin envoy came, daily he carted heavy treasures to Wuxing, as a plan for escape;
translations.idiomatic: ever since the Jin emissaries arrived, he has been shipping his treasures daily to Wuxing, laying plans for flight;

sentences.zh: 陰養惡少，私置兵甲；

translations.literal: he secretly raised wicked youths and privately stockpiled weapons and armor;
translations.idiomatic: he secretly maintained bands of ruffians and illegally stockpiled arms and armor;

sentences.zh: 受富民金，薦為閤職；

translations.literal: he accepted gold from wealthy men and recommended them for Gate offices;
translations.idiomatic: he took bribes from wealthy men and secured them posts in the palace gates;

sentences.zh: 州縣大獄，以賂解免；

translations.literal: major cases in prefectures and counties were cleared through bribes;
translations.idiomatic: major criminal cases in prefectures and counties were dismissed through his bribes;

sentences.zh: 誣姊姦淫，加之黥隸；

translations.literal: he falsely accused his elder sisters of fornication and had them tattooed and enslaved;
translations.idiomatic: he falsely charged his elder sisters with incest and had them tattooed and enslaved;

sentences.zh: 又于諸處佛寺建立生祠，凡名山大刹所有，大半入其家。

translations.literal: he also built living shrines to himself at Buddhist temples everywhere; most of the estates belonging to famous mountains and great monasteries passed into his household.
translations.idiomatic: He also erected living shrines to himself at Buddhist temples across the land, and seized most of the estates belonging to famous mountains and great monasteries.

sentences.zh: 此特舉其大者，其餘擢發未足數也。」

translations.literal: These are only the major offenses; the rest, even counted hair by hair, would not suffice to enumerate."
translations.idiomatic: These are only the worst of his crimes—the rest are too numerous to count."

sentences.zh: 奏入，詔繼先福州居住。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered Jixian to reside at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor ordered Wang Jixian to take up residence at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其子安道，武泰軍承宣使；

translations.literal: His son Andao was an Inspecting Commissioner of the Wutai Army;
translations.idiomatic: His son Andao, an inspecting commissioner of the Wutai Army;

sentences.zh: 守道，朝議大夫、直徽猷閣；

translations.literal: Shoudao was Gentleman for Discussion at Court and Rectifier of the Huiyou Pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: Shoudao, Gentleman for Discussion at Court and rectifier of the Huiyou Pavilion;

sentences.zh: 悅道朝奉郎、直秘閣；

translations.literal: Yuedao was Attendant Gentleman and Rectifier of the Secret Pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: Yuedao, Attendant Gentleman and rectifier of the Secret Pavilion;

sentences.zh: 孫錡，承議郎、直秘閣，並勒停。

translations.literal: his grandson Jin was Gentleman for Discussion and Rectifier of the Secret Pavilion—all were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: and his grandson Jin, Gentleman for Discussion and rectifier of the Secret Pavilion—all were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 放還良家子為奴婢者凡百餘人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred persons of good families who had been made slaves and maidservants were released.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred persons of good family who had been enslaved as servants were freed.

sentences.zh: 籍其貲以千萬計，鬻其田園及金銀，並隸御前激賞庫。

translations.literal: His assets, reckoned in the tens of millions, were registered; his fields, gardens, gold, and silver were sold off and all entered the Imperial Stimulating Rewards Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: His assets, reckoned in the tens of millions, were inventoried; his estates, gold, and silver were sold, and the proceeds were placed in the Imperial Stimulating Rewards Treasury.

sentences.zh: 其海舟付李寶，天下稱快。

translations.literal: His seagoing vessels were handed over to Li Bao, and the realm rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: His seagoing vessels were turned over to Li Bao, to universal acclaim.

sentences.zh: 方繼先之怙寵奸法，帝亦知之，故晚年以公議廢之，遂不復起。

translations.literal: While Jixian had been arrogant in favor and lawless, the emperor had known it as well; therefore in his later years he was removed through public opinion and never rose again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long known of Jixian's arrogance in favor and his lawlessness; in his later years he was removed through public outcry and never returned to power.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，詔任便居住，毋至行在。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong acceded, an edict allowed him to reside where he pleased and forbade him to come to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, an edict permitted him to live where he chose and forbade him to approach the court.

sentences.zh: 淳熙八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chunxi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of the Chunxi reign (1181).

sentences.zh: 龍大淵 附

translations.literal: Long Dayuan — appendix
translations.idiomatic: Long Dayuan (supplementary biography)

sentences.zh: 曾覿，字純甫，其先汴人也。

translations.literal: Zeng Di, style Chunfu, was originally from Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Di, courtesy name Chunfu, was a native of Bian (Kaifeng).

sentences.zh: 用父任補官。

translations.literal: He entered office through his father's yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He received his initial appointment through his father's yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十年，以寄班祗候與龍大淵同為建王內知客。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing, as a Palace Attendant Duty Officer he served together with Long Dayuan as inner intimates of the Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing (1160), he and Long Dayuan, both palace attendant duty officers, served as inner intimates of the Prince of Jian.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，大淵自左武大夫除樞密副都承旨，而覿自武翼郎除帶禦器械、幹辦皇城司。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong received the abdication, Dayuan was promoted from Left Martial Grand Master to Deputy Chief Palace Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, while Di was promoted from Martial Wing Lang to Bearer of the Imperial Arms and Administrator of the Imperial City Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong accepted the abdication, Dayuan rose from Left Martial Grand Master to deputy chief palace secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, while Di rose from Martial Wing Lang to bearer of the imperial arms and administrator of the Imperial City Bureau.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫劉度入對，首言二人潛邸舊人，待之不可無節度；

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee Liu Du entered audience and first said that the two men were old associates from the hidden residence and that they must not be treated without restraint;
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee Liu Du, on entering audience, urged first that the two were old associates from the prince's hidden residence and must not be indulged without restraint;

sentences.zh: 又因進故事，論京房、石顯事。

translations.literal: he also cited historical precedents in discussion, adducing the cases of Jing Fang and Shi Xian.
translations.idiomatic: he also cited historical precedents, invoking the cases of Jing Fang and Shi Xian.

sentences.zh: 大淵遂除知閣門事，而覿除權知閣門事。

translations.literal: Dayuan was then appointed Director of the Gate, and Di Acting Director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan was then appointed director of the Gate, and Di acting director of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 度言：「臣欲退之，而陛下進之，何面目尚為諫官？

translations.literal: Du said: "Your servant wished to have them removed, yet Your Majesty has advanced them—what face remains for me to serve as remonstrance official?
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "I sought to have them removed, yet Your Majesty has promoted them—how can I still hold my face as a remonstrance official?

sentences.zh: 乞賜貶黜。」

translations.literal: I beg to be demoted and dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be demoted and dismissed."

sentences.zh: 中書舍人張震繳其命至再，出知紹興府。

translations.literal: Palace Drafter Zhang Zhen returned the appointment twice, and Du was sent out as prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Drafter Zhang Zhen returned the appointment twice, and Liu Du was sent out as prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史胡沂亦論二人市權，既而給舍金安節、周必大再封還錄黃。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Hu Yi also criticized the two for trafficking in power; thereafter Drafting Gentleman Jin Anjie and Zhou Bida again sealed and returned the yellow record.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor Hu Yi also denounced the two for trafficking in power; soon Drafting Gentlemen Jin Anjie and Zhou Bida again sealed and returned the yellow record.

sentences.zh: 時張燾新拜參政，亦欲以大淵、覿決去就，力言之，帝不納。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Tao had newly been appointed participating administrator; he too wished to settle the matter of Dayuan and Di by their removal, spoke forcefully, and the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tao had just been appointed participating administrator and likewise sought to settle the fate of Dayuan and Di by their removal; he spoke forcefully, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 燾辭去，遂以內祠兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Tao resigned and was given an inner temple post with concurrent appointment as imperial reader.
translations.idiomatic: Tao resigned and was given an inner temple post with concurrent appointment as imperial reader.

sentences.zh: 劉度奪言職，權工部侍郎，而二人仍知閣門事。

translations.literal: Liu Du was stripped of his remonstrance office and made acting Vice Minister of Works, while the two men still held the Gate directorships.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Du was stripped of his remonstrance office and made acting vice minister of Works, while the two still held the Gate directorships.

sentences.zh: 必大格除目不下，尋與祠，二人除命亦寢。

translations.literal: Bida withheld the appointment documents and would not issue them; soon he too received a temple post, and the two men's appointments also lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bida withheld the appointment documents and would not issue them; soon he too received a temple post, and the appointments of the two lapsed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒以大淵為宜州觀察使、知閣門事；

translations.literal: Before long, Dayuan was finally made Observation Commissioner of Yizhou and Director of the Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Dayuan was finally made observation commissioner of Yizhou and director of the Gate;

sentences.zh: 覿，文州刺史、權知閣門：皆兼皇城司。

translations.literal: Di was made Prefect of Wenzhou and Acting Director of the Gate—both concurrently held the Imperial City Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Di was made prefect of Wenzhou and acting director of the Gate—both concurrently held the Imperial City Bureau.

sentences.zh: 不數月間，除命四變。

translations.literal: Within a few months their appointments changed four times.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months their appointments changed four times.

sentences.zh: 劉度出知建寧府，尋放罷。

translations.literal: Liu Du was sent out as prefect of Jianning and soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Du was sent out as prefect of Jianning and soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 群臣既以言二人得罪去，侍御史周操章十五上，不報。

translations.literal: Since the ministers had already been punished and removed for speaking of the two men, Attendant Censor Zhou Cao submitted fifteen memorials and received no response.
translations.idiomatic: After ministers had already been punished and removed for criticizing the two, Attendant Censor Zhou Cao submitted fifteen memorials and received no response.

sentences.zh: 自是覿與大淵勢張甚，士大夫之寡恥者潛附麗之。

translations.literal: From then on Di and Dayuan grew very powerful; scholars lacking shame secretly attached themselves to them.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Di and Dayuan grew formidable in power, and shameless scholars quietly attached themselves to them.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗令大淵撫慰兩淮將士，侍御史王十朋言大淵銜命撫師，非出朝廷論選之公，有輕國體。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered Dayuan to console the officers and soldiers of the Two Huai; Attendant Censor Wang Shipeng said that Dayuan, bearing the mandate to console the armies, had not been chosen through the court's public deliberation—a slight to the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered Dayuan to console the officers and soldiers of the Two Huai; Attendant Censor Wang Shipeng said that Dayuan, bearing a mandate to console the armies, had not been chosen through the court's public deliberation—a slight to national dignity.

sentences.zh: 時又有內侍押班梁珂者，三人表裏用事。

translations.literal: At the time there was also the inner attendant and duty officer Liang Ke; the three men worked in concert inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was also the inner attendant and duty officer Liang Ke; the three worked in concert inside and out.

sentences.zh: 及珂以罪出，右正言龔茂良入對，首論：「二人害政甚珂百倍，陛下罷行一政事，進退一人才，必掠美自歸，謂為己力。

translations.literal: When Ke was removed for crime, Right Remonstrance Official Gong Maoliang entered audience and first argued: "The harm these two do to government is a hundred times greater than Ke's; whenever Your Majesty abolishes a policy or advances or dismisses a man of talent, they must seize the credit and claim it as their own doing.
translations.idiomatic: When Ke was removed for crime, Right Remonstrance Official Gong Maoliang, on entering audience, argued first: "These two harm government a hundredfold more than Ke; whenever Your Majesty abolishes a policy or advances or dismisses a talent, they seize the credit and claim it as their own doing.

sentences.zh: 或時有少過，昌言於外，謂嘗爭之而不見聽。

translations.literal: If at times there was some small fault, they proclaimed it abroad, saying they had argued against it but were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: If there was some small fault, they proclaimed abroad that they had argued against it but were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 群臣章疏留中未出，間得窺見，出以語人。

translations.literal: Memorials from the ministers that were held in the palace and not issued—they sometimes glimpsed them and disclosed them to others.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from ministers held in the palace and not issued—they sometimes glimpsed them and disclosed them to others.

sentences.zh: 有司條陳利害，示以副封，公然可否。

translations.literal: When offices submitted items on benefits and harms, they were shown the duplicate seal and openly approved or rejected them.
translations.idiomatic: When offices submitted analyses of benefits and harms, they were shown the duplicate seal and openly approved or rejected them.

sentences.zh: 若夫交通賄賂，幹求差遣，特其小者耳。

translations.literal: As for taking bribes and soliciting appointments, those were only the lesser matters.
translations.idiomatic: Bribery and solicitation of appointments were only the lesser of their offenses.

sentences.zh: 願特出威斷，並行罷去。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty especially to issue a resolute decree and remove them both at once."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue a resolute decree and remove them both at once."

sentences.zh: 先是，江、浙大水，詔侍從、台諫陳闕政。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiang and Zhe had suffered great floods; an edict ordered attendants and remonstrance and censorial officials to state governmental failings.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiang and Zhe had suffered severe flooding; an edict ordered attendants and remonstrance and censorial officials to report governmental failings.

sentences.zh: 著作郎劉夙上封事曰：「陛下與覿、大淵輩觴詠唱酬，字而不名。

translations.literal: Authoring Gentleman Liu Su submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Your Majesty drinks and composes verse with Di, Dayuan, and their like, addressing them by style name and not by office.
translations.idiomatic: Authoring Gentleman Liu Su submitted a sealed memorial: "Your Majesty drinks and composes verse with Di, Dayuan, and their like, addressing them by style name rather than by office.

sentences.zh: 罷宰相，易大將，待其言而後決。

translations.literal: You dismiss a chief minister or replace a great general only after waiting for their word before deciding.
translations.idiomatic: You dismiss a chief minister or replace a great general only after waiting for their word.

sentences.zh: 嚴法守，裁僥倖，當自宮掖近侍始。」

translations.literal: To enforce the law strictly and cut off favoritism should begin with those close at hand in the inner palace."
translations.idiomatic: Strict enforcement of law and cutting off favoritism should begin with those close at hand in the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 茂良時為監察御史，亦言：「水至陰，其占為女寵，為嬖佞，為小人，蓋專指左右近習也。」

translations.literal: Maoliang was then investigating censor and also said: "Water is utmost yin; its omen is female favor, flatterers, and petty men—it plainly points to those close at hand on the left and right."
translations.idiomatic: Maoliang was then investigating censor and also said, "Water is utmost yin; its omen is female favor, flatterers, and petty men—it plainly points to those close at hand on the left and right."

sentences.zh: 帝諭以二人皆潛邸舊人，非近習比；

translations.literal: The emperor instructed them that the two were old men from the hidden residence and were not to be compared with recent intimates;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that the two were old associates from the hidden residence and were not to be compared with recent intimates;

sentences.zh: 且俱有文學，敢諫諍，杜門不出，不預外事，宜退而訪問。

translations.literal: moreover both were literarily accomplished, dared to remonstrate, kept their doors closed and did not go out, and did not interfere in outside affairs—one should withdraw and inquire of them.
translations.idiomatic: moreover both were literarily accomplished, dared to remonstrate, kept their doors closed, did not meddle in outside affairs—one should withdraw and consult them instead.

sentences.zh: 茂良再上疏言：「德宗不知盧杞之奸邪，此其所以奸邪也。

translations.literal: Maoliang again submitted a memorial saying: "Suzong did not know Lu Qi's treachery—that is precisely why Qi was treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Maoliang submitted again: "Emperor Dezong did not know Lu Qi's treachery—that is precisely why Qi was treacherous.

sentences.zh: 大淵、覿所為，行道之人能言之，特陛下未之覺耳。」

translations.literal: What Dayuan and Di do, travelers on the road can speak of it—it is only that Your Majesty has not yet perceived it."
translations.idiomatic: What Dayuan and Di do, travelers on the road can recount—it is only that Your Majesty has not yet perceived it."

sentences.zh: 疏入不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, no response was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted; no response was issued.

sentences.zh: 茂良待罪，除太常少卿，五辭不拜，出知建寧府。

translations.literal: Maoliang awaited punishment; he was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, declined five times and did not accept, and was sent out as prefect of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Maoliang awaited punishment; he was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, declined five times, and was sent out as prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 一日，右史洪邁過參政陳俊卿曰：「聞將除右史，邁遷西掖，信乎？」

translations.literal: One day Right Historian Hong Mai called on Participating Administrator Chen Junqing and said: "I hear a right historian is to be appointed and Mai is to move to the western drafting office—is it true?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Right Historian Hong Mai called on Participating Administrator Chen Junqing and said, "I hear a right historian is to be appointed and I am to move to the western drafting office—is it true?"

sentences.zh: 俊卿曰：「何自得之？」

translations.literal: Junqing said: "How did you learn of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Junqing said, "How did you learn of it?"

sentences.zh: 邁以二人告。

translations.literal: Mai told him it was the two men.
translations.idiomatic: Mai said the two men had told him.

sentences.zh: 俊卿即以語宰相葉顒、魏杞，而己獨奏之，且以邁語質之帝前，帝怒，即出二人於外。

translations.literal: Junqing at once informed Chief Ministers Ye Yu and Wei Qi, while he alone memorialized the throne, and in the emperor's presence confronted him with Mai's words; the emperor was angry and immediately sent the two men outside.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing at once informed chief ministers Ye Yu and Wei Qi, while he alone memorialized the throne and confronted the emperor with Mai's words; the emperor was enraged and immediately sent the two outside.

sentences.zh: 於是遷大淵為江東總管，覿為淮西副總管，中外快之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dayuan was transferred as Jiangdong Commander-in-Chief and Di as Huai West Deputy Commander-in-Chief, to the joy of court and country.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan was then transferred as Jiangdong commander-in-chief and Di as Huai West deputy commander-in-chief, to the joy of court and country.

sentences.zh: 尋改大淵浙東、覿福建。

translations.literal: Soon Dayuan was changed to Zhe East and Di to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dayuan was reassigned to Zhe East and Di to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾道四年，大淵死，覿尚在福建。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiandao, Dayuan died; Di was still in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiandao (1168), Dayuan died; Di was still in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 帝憐，欲召之，樞密劉珙奏曰：「此曹奴隸爾，厚賜之可也。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and wished to summon him; Military Affairs Commissioner Liu Gong memorialized: "These fellows are mere slaves—generous gifts are enough.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied him and wished to recall him; Military Affairs Commissioner Liu Gong memorialized, "These fellows are mere slaves—generous gifts are enough.

sentences.zh: 引以自近而待以賓友，使得與聞政事，非所以增聖德、整朝綱也。」

translations.literal: To draw them close and treat them as guest-friends, allowing them to hear of government affairs, is not the way to increase sagely virtue or rectify court discipline."
translations.idiomatic: To draw them near and treat them as guest-friends, allowing them to hear of government affairs, is not the way to increase sagely virtue or rectify court discipline."

sentences.zh: 帝納珙言，命遂寢。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted Gong's words and the order lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Gong's counsel and the summons lapsed.

sentences.zh: 既而覿垂滿，俊卿恐其入，預請以浙東總管處之。

translations.literal: Before long Di's term was nearing completion; Junqing feared he would enter the capital and beforehand requested that he be placed as Zhe East Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Di's term was nearing completion; Junqing, fearing he would enter the capital, beforehand requested that he be placed as Zhe East commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 台臣上疏論之，不報。

translations.literal: Censorial officials submitted memorials on the matter; no response.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials submitted memorials; no response.

sentences.zh: 太學錄魏掞之亟上封事論列，且見俊卿切責之，掞之得台州教官以出。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy Recorder Wei Dashan urgently submitted a sealed memorial criticizing him and also saw Junqing to rebuke him sharply; Dashan received a teaching post at Taizhou and left.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Academy Recorder Wei Dashan urgently submitted a sealed memorial criticizing the appointment and also saw Junqing to rebuke him sharply; Dashan received a teaching post at Taizhou and left.

sentences.zh: 覿至龍山已久，伺掞之去，然後入國門。

translations.literal: Di had been at Longshan a long time; he waited until Dashan had gone, then entered the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: Di had lingered at Longshan a long time; he waited until Dashan had gone, then entered the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 會虞允文使蜀還，與俊卿同奏覿不可留。

translations.literal: When Yu Yunwen returned from his mission to Shu, he joined Junqing in memorializing that Di must not be retained.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yunwen returned from his mission to Shu, he joined Junqing in memorializing that Di must not be retained.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然，留則累朕。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is—if he is retained it will burden Us."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So it is—to retain him would burden Us.

sentences.zh: 卒除浙東副總管。

translations.literal: In the end he was made Zhe East Deputy Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Di was made Zhe East deputy commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以墨詔進覿一官為觀察使，中書舍人繳還，不因事除拜，必有人言。

translations.literal: Before long, by informal edict Di was advanced one rank to observation commissioner; the palace drafter returned the appointment, saying that appointments not tied to some affair would surely draw criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, by informal edict Di was advanced one rank to observation commissioner; the palace drafter returned the appointment, saying appointments not tied to some affair would surely draw criticism.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 俊卿曰：「不爾，亦須有名。」

translations.literal: Junqing said: "If not, there must still be a pretext."
translations.idiomatic: Junqing said, "If not, there must still be a pretext."

sentences.zh: 會汪大猷為賀金正旦使，俾覿副之。

translations.literal: When Wang Dayou was made envoy to congratulate the Jin on New Year's Day, Di was made his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dayou was made envoy to congratulate the Jin on New Year's Day, Di was appointed his deputy.

sentences.zh: 比還，遷一秩，而竟申浙東之命，且戒閣門吏趣朝辭，覿由是怏怏而去。

translations.literal: When they returned, he was advanced one grade, yet in the end the Zhe East appointment was carried out; moreover the Gate officers were instructed to hurry his court leave-taking audience, and Di departed in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: On their return he was advanced one grade, yet in the end the Zhe East appointment stood; the Gate officers were instructed to hurry his leave-taking audience, and Di departed in resentment.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，俊卿罷政。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, Junqing left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year, Junqing left office.

sentences.zh: 十月，覿以京祠召。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Di was summoned on a capital temple post.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Di was summoned on a capital temple post.

sentences.zh: 七年，立皇太子，覿以伴讀勞，升承宣使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the heir apparent was installed, Di was raised to inspecting commissioner for his labors as companion reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the heir apparent was installed, Di was raised to inspecting commissioner for his labors as companion reader.

sentences.zh: 八年，姚憲為賀金國尊號使，覿副之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Yao Xian was made envoy to congratulate the Jin on their honorific title; Di was his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Yao Xian was made envoy to congratulate the Jin on their honorific title; Di served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 歸，除武泰軍節度使，提舉萬壽觀。

translations.literal: On his return he was made military commissioner of the Wutai Army and superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made military commissioner of the Wutai Army and superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年，除開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunxi, he was made Commissioner with the same powers as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunxi (1174), he was made commissioner with the same powers as the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 四年，覿欲以文資官其子孫，帝遣中使至省中具使相奏補法，龔茂良時以參政行丞相事，遽以文武官各隨本色蔭補法繳進，覿大怒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Di wished to obtain civil-service appointments for his sons and grandsons; the emperor sent a palace envoy to the Secretariat to obtain the regulations on memorial appointment for chief ministers; Gong Maoliang was then participating administrator acting as chief minister and hastily submitted the regulations on yin appointment for civil and military officials according to their original categories; Di was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Di wished to obtain civil-service appointments for his sons and grandsons; the emperor sent a palace envoy to the Secretariat for the regulations on memorial appointment for chief ministers; Gong Maoliang, then participating administrator acting as chief minister, hastily submitted the regulations on yin appointment for civil and military officials according to their original categories; Di was furious.

sentences.zh: 茂良退朝，覿從騎不避，茂良執而撻之，待罪乞出，不許。

translations.literal: When Maoliang left court, Di's mounted attendants did not yield; Maoliang seized and flogged them, awaited punishment and begged to leave office, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Maoliang left court, Di's mounted attendants did not yield; Maoliang seized and flogged them, submitted himself for punishment and begged to leave office, and was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 戶部員外郎謝廓然忽賜出身，除侍御史。

translations.literal: Ministry of Revenue Outer Section Member Xie Kuoran was suddenly granted initial status and made Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Revenue outer section member Xie Kuoran was suddenly granted initial status and made attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 廓然首論茂良，以資政殿學士知鎮江；

translations.literal: Kuoran first attacked Maoliang, who was made Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Virtue and prefect of Zhenjiang;
translations.idiomatic: Kuoran first attacked Maoliang, who was made academician of the Hall for Cultivating Virtue and prefect of Zhenjiang;

sentences.zh: 章再上，鐫罷；

translations.literal: when the memorial was submitted again, he was engraved and dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: when the memorial was submitted again, he was engraved on the stone and dismissed;

sentences.zh: 言之不已，貶英州，皆覿所使也。

translations.literal: when he spoke without cease, he was demoted to Yingzhou—all at Di's instigation.
translations.idiomatic: when he would not cease, he was demoted to Yingzhou—all at Di's instigation.

sentences.zh: 覿前雖預事，未敢肆，至是責逐大臣，士始側目重足矣。

translations.literal: Though Di had earlier taken part in affairs, he had not dared to act recklessly; only now did he drive out great ministers, and scholars began to regard him with sidelong eyes and deep apprehension.
translations.idiomatic: Though Di had earlier taken part in affairs, he had not dared to act recklessly; only now did he drive out great ministers, and scholars began to regard him with sidelong eyes and deep apprehension.

sentences.zh: 廓然既以擅權罪茂良，從班有韓彥古者，覿之姻，廓然之黨，遂獻議助之，使人主疑大臣而信近習，至是益甚。

translations.literal: After Kuoran had condemned Maoliang for usurping power, among the court cohort was Han Yanggu, Di's in-law and Kuoran's partisan; he then offered counsel to assist them, causing the sovereign to doubt great ministers and trust close intimates—a tendency that grew worse from this point.
translations.idiomatic: After Kuoran had condemned Maoliang for usurping power, among the court cohort was Han Yanggu, Di's in-law and Kuoran's partisan; he then offered counsel to assist them, causing the sovereign to doubt great ministers and trust close intimates—a tendency that grew worse thereafter.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，帝幸佑聖觀，召宰臣史浩及覿同賜酒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, the emperor visited the You Sheng Abbey and summoned Chief Minister Shi Hao and Di to share wine together.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year, the emperor visited the You Sheng Abbey and summoned Chief Minister Shi Hao and Di to share wine together.

sentences.zh: 是歲，加覿少保、醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: That year, Di was made Junior Guardian and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Di was made junior guardian and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 時周必大當草制，人謂其必不肯從，及制出，乃有「敬故在尊賢之上」之語，士論惜之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Bida was to draft the edict; men said he would surely refuse, yet when the edict appeared it contained the phrase "honoring the old ranks above honoring the worthy"—scholarly opinion lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhou Bida was to draft the edict; men said he would surely refuse, yet when the edict appeared it contained the phrase "honoring the old ranks above honoring the worthy"—scholarly opinion lamented it.

sentences.zh: 覿始與龍大淵相朋，及大淵死，則與王抃、甘昪相蟠結，文武要職多出三人之門。

translations.literal: Di had at first been allied with Long Dayuan; after Dayuan died he coiled together with Wang Bian and Gan Bian, and important civil and military posts mostly issued from the three men's doors.
translations.idiomatic: Di had at first been allied with Long Dayuan; after Dayuan died he intertwined with Wang Bian and Gan Bian, and important civil and military posts mostly issued from the three men's doors.

sentences.zh: 葉衡自小官十年至宰相。

translations.literal: Ye Heng rose from a minor office in ten years to chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Heng rose from a minor office in ten years to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 徐本中由小使臣積階至刺史、知閣門事，換文資為右文殿修撰、樞密都承旨、賜三品服，俄為浙西提刑，尋以集英殿修撰奉內祠。

translations.literal: Xu Benzhong, from a minor envoy, accumulated ranks to prefect and Director of the Gate; he exchanged his military status for civil rank as Academician of the Right Culture Hall, chief palace secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and grant of third-rank robes; soon he was Huai West investigating commissioner for punishments; shortly he was made Academician of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and received an inner temple post.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Benzhong, from a minor envoy, accumulated ranks to prefect and director of the Gate; he exchanged military status for civil rank as academician of the Right Culture Hall, chief palace secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and grant of third-rank robes; soon he was Huai West investigating commissioner for punishments; shortly thereafter he was made academician of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and received an inner temple post.

sentences.zh: 是二人者，皆覿所進也。

translations.literal: Both these two men were all advanced by Di.
translations.idiomatic: Both men had been promoted through Zeng Di's patronage.

sentences.zh: 著作郎胡晉臣因轉對，極論近習怙權之害，遂出知漢州。

translations.literal: Composition Officer Hu Jinchen, on a rotation audience, spoke at length on the harm of close intimates clinging to power, and was then sent out as prefect of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Composition Officer Hu Jinchen, during a rotation audience, spoke forcefully against close intimates hoarding power and was sent out to serve as prefect of Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 南康守朱熹應詔上書，其言尤力，有曰：「一二近習之人，蠱惑陛下心志，所謂宰相、師傅、賓友、諫諍之臣，或反出入其門牆，承望其風旨。」

translations.literal: Nankang prefect Zhu Xi, responding to an imperial summons, submitted a memorial; his words were especially forceful, saying: 'One or two men among the close intimates bewitch Your Majesty's mind; the so-called chief ministers, tutors, friends, and remonstrating officials—or on the contrary pass in and out of their gates and walls, looking to catch their intent.'
translations.idiomatic: Nankang Prefect Zhu Xi answered the imperial summons with a memorial whose language was especially blunt: 'A handful of close intimates have beguiled Your Majesty's mind. The men who ought to be your chief ministers, tutors, friends, and remonstrators instead come and go at their gates, eager to catch their drift.'

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝怒，諭令分析，丞相趙雄言之，事遂止。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was angry and ordered that it be analyzed item by item; Chief Minister Zhao Xiong spoke on the matter, and the affair then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was furious and ordered a point-by-point rebuttal; Chief Minister Zhao Xiong intervened, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 陳俊卿守金陵，過闕入見，首言曾覿、王抃招權納賂，薦進人才，皆以中批行之。

translations.literal: Chen Junqing, holding Nanjing, passed the capital to enter audience and first spoke of Zeng Di and Wang Bian's recruiting power and taking bribes, advancing talent—all carried out by central rescripts.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junqing, prefect of Nanjing, stopped at court for an audience and opened by accusing Zeng Di and Wang Bian of trading in power and bribes, pushing favorites through imperial rescripts.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「瑣細差遣，或勉循之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'For trifling assignments, one may reluctantly follow them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'For petty appointments I might go along.

sentences.zh: 至於近上之除，此輩何敢預。」

translations.literal: As for appointments close to the throne, how would these men dare to intervene.'
translations.idiomatic: But for posts near the throne—how could such men dare to meddle?'

sentences.zh: 俊卿入辭，又曰：「向來士大夫奔覿、抃之門，十才一二，尚畏人知；

translations.literal: Junqing on his leave-taking audience again said: 'Formerly scholars rushed to Di's and Bian's doors—only one or two in ten, still fearing that others would know;
translations.idiomatic: On his farewell audience Junqing added, 'Once, perhaps one scholar in ten would court Di or Bian, and even then in secret;

sentences.zh: 今則公然趨附，十已八九，大非朝廷美事也。」

translations.literal: now they openly hurry to attach themselves—eight or nine in ten; this is greatly not a fine affair for the court.'
translations.idiomatic: now eight or nine in ten do so openly. That is no credit to the court.'

sentences.zh: 帝感悟。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to understanding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point.

sentences.zh: 覿用事二十年，權震中外，至於譖逐大臣，貶死嶺外。

translations.literal: Di had held power for twenty years, his authority shaking court and countryside, even to slandering and driving out great ministers and banishing them to death beyond the Lingnan passes.
translations.idiomatic: Di had wielded power for twenty years, his influence felt inside and outside the court; he had slandered and expelled great ministers and sent men to die in exile beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 自是浸覺其奸，嘗謂左右曰：「曾覿誤我不少。」

translations.literal: From this time he gradually perceived Di's treachery and once said to those beside him: 'Zeng Di has misled me no little.'
translations.idiomatic: He gradually came to see Di's deceit and once told his attendants, 'Zeng Di has led me badly astray.'

sentences.zh: 遂稍疏覿。

translations.literal: He then slightly distanced Di.
translations.idiomatic: He began to keep Di at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 覿憂恚，疽發於背。

translations.literal: Di, anxious and resentful, developed a carbuncle on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Di, anxious and bitter, developed a carbuncle on his back.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，侍帝宴於翠寒堂，退為記以進。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year he attended the emperor's banquet at the Cuihan Hall; on retiring he composed a record and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year he attended the emperor's banquet in the Cuihan Hall; afterward he wrote an account and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 十二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died.

sentences.zh: 於是凡前論覿得罪者皆錄贈，胡晉臣起至執政，魏掞之贈直秘閣，龔茂良悉還其職名恩數雲。

translations.literal: Thereupon all who had earlier spoken against Di and been punished were recorded for posthumous honors; Hu Jinchen was raised to participating administrator; Wei Yan was posthumously granted Direct Academician of the Secretariat; Gong Maoliang had all his offices, titles, and favors restored, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: Then everyone who had earlier been punished for criticizing Di was posthumously honored; Hu Jinchen was recalled to the council; Wei Yan was posthumously made direct academician of the Secretariat; Gong Maoliang had his offices, titles, and privileges fully restored, and the like.

sentences.zh: 張說，開封人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shuo was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuo was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父公裕，省吏也，為和州防禦使，建炎初有軍功。

translations.literal: His father Gongyu was a provincial clerk who became defense commissioner of Hezhou and had military merit at the beginning of the Jianyan era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Gongyu had been a provincial clerk, became defense commissioner of Hezhou, and won distinction in the opening years of the Jianyan era.

sentences.zh: 說受父任為右職，娶壽聖皇后女弟，由是累遷知閣門事。

translations.literal: Shuo received his father's appointment as a right-rank post, married the younger sister of the Empress Dowager Shousheng, and by this was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo inherited his father's right-rank appointment, married a younger sister of Empress Dowager Shousheng, and rose step by step to director of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 隆興初，兼樞密副都承旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longxing he also served as deputy chief palace secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Longxing era he also served as deputy chief palace secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾道初，為都承旨，加明州觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiandao he became chief palace secretary and was made observation commissioner of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Qiandao era he became chief palace secretary and was made observation commissioner of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，除簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year he was made Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year he was appointed deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時起復劉珙同知樞密院，珙恥與之同命，力辭不拜，命既下，朝論譁然不平，莫敢頌言於朝者。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Qi was recalled to serve as associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Qi was ashamed to share the appointment with him and strenuously declined; once the order was issued, court opinion was in an uproar and none dared praise it at court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi had just been recalled as associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Qi was ashamed to share rank with Shuo and refused the post. Once the order went out, opinion seethed at court and no one dared voice approval.

sentences.zh: 惟左司員外郎張栻在經筵力言之，中書舍人范成大不草詞。

translations.literal: Only Left Division Outer Section Member Zhang Shi spoke forcefully in the classics lecture hall; Drafting Attendant Fan Chengda would not draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Shi of the left division spoke bluntly in the classics lecture hall; drafting attendant Fan Chengda refused to draft the appointment edict.

sentences.zh: 尋除說安遠軍節度使，奉祠歸第。

translations.literal: Shortly Shuo was made military commissioner of the Anyuan Army and received a temple post to return to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shuo was made military commissioner of the Anyuan Army and sent home on a temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 不數月，出栻知袁州。

translations.literal: Within a few months Zhang Shi was sent out as prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Zhang Shi was sent out as prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 說既奉祠，語人曰：「張左司平時不相樂，固也。

translations.literal: After Shuo received his temple post he said to others: 'Left Division Member Zhang and I were never on good terms—that is so.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his temple post Shuo remarked, 'Left Division Member Zhang and I were never friendly—that much is true.

sentences.zh: 范致能亦胡為見攻？」

translations.literal: Why did Fan Zhineng also join in attacking me?'
translations.idiomatic: But why did Fan Zhineng turn on me as well?'

sentences.zh: 指所坐亭材植曰：「是皆致能所惠也。」

translations.literal: He pointed at the timber and plantings of the pavilion where he sat and said: 'These were all Zhineng's gifts.'
translations.idiomatic: He gestured at the timber and plantings of his pavilion: 'All of this came from Zhineng.'

sentences.zh: 八年二月，復自安遠軍節度使提舉萬壽觀，簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he was again made from military commissioner of the Anyuan Army superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he was again raised from military commissioner of the Anyuan Army to superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 侍御史李衡、右正言王希呂交章論之，起居郎莫濟不書錄黃，直院周必大不草答詔，於是命權給事中姚憲書讀行下，命翰林學士王暼嚴草答詔，未幾，暼嚴升學士承旨，憲贈出身，為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Li Heng and Remonstrator Wang Xilu submitted successive memorials attacking him; Diary Attendant Mo Ji would not record the yellow copy; Academician Zhou Bida would not draft the response edict; thereupon the order went to Acting Drafting Attendant Yao Xian to read and issue it, and Hanlin Academician Wang Yanmo to draft the response; before long Yanmo was promoted to chief academician, Xian was granted initial status and made remonstrating grand master.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant censor Li Heng and remonstrator Wang Xilu attacked him in successive memorials; diary attendant Mo Ji refused to record the yellow copy; academician Zhou Bida refused to draft the reply edict. The order then went to acting drafting attendant Yao Xian to read and promulgate it, and Hanlin academician Wang Yanmo to draft the reply; soon Yanmo was promoted chief academician, Xian was granted initial status and made remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 詔希呂合黨邀名，持論反覆，責遠小監當。

translations.literal: An edict condemned Xilu for forming factions to seek fame and reversing his positions, and demoted him to a distant minor supervisory post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned Wang Xilu for faction-seeking and flip-flopping and demoted him to a distant minor supervisory post.

sentences.zh: 衡素與說厚，所言亦婉，止罷言職，遷左史，而濟、必大皆與在外宮觀，日下出國門。

translations.literal: Heng had long been close to Shuo and his words were also mild; he was only removed from his remonstrating post and promoted to left historiographer, while Ji and Bida were both sent to outer temple posts and ordered to leave the capital the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Heng had long been friendly with Shuo and his language was mild; he merely lost his remonstrating post and was made left historiographer, while Ji and Bida were both sent to outer temple posts and ordered out of the capital that day.

sentences.zh: 國子司業劉焞移書責宰相，言說不當用，即為言者所論，出為江西轉運判官。

translations.literal: National University Vice Director Liu Xun sent a letter reproaching the chief minister, saying Shuo should not be employed, and was at once attacked by the speakers and sent out as transport judge of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: National University vice director Liu Xun wrote reproaching the chief minister for employing Shuo; critics at once attacked him and he was sent out as Jiangxi transport judge.

sentences.zh: 於是說勢赫然，無敢攖之者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shuo's power blazed conspicuously and none dared contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo's power now blazed, and no one dared challenge him.

sentences.zh: 九年春，說露章薦濟、必大，於是二人皆予郡，必大卒不出。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year Shuo openly memorialized recommending Ji and Bida; thereupon both were granted prefectures, but Bida in the end did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year Shuo openly memorialized to recommend Ji and Bida; both were given prefectures, though Bida never took up his post.

sentences.zh: 先是，南丹州莫延葚表乞就宜州市馬，比橫山省三十程，說在樞筦以聞，樞屬有論其不便，說不聽。

translations.literal: Earlier, the chieftain of Nandan, Mo Yanqin, had memorialized asking to purchase horses at Yizhou city, thirty stages nearer than Hengshan; when Shuo was in the Bureau he reported it; staff under the bureau argued it was unwise and Shuo would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Nandan chieftain Mo Yanqin had asked to buy horses at Yizhou city—thirty stages closer than Hengshan. While Shuo sat in the Bureau he reported the request; staff argued against it, but he would not hear them.

sentences.zh: 說既貶，遂罷其議。

translations.literal: After Shuo was demoted, the proposal was then abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shuo fell, the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 說又嘗建議欲郎官、卿監通差武臣，中書舍人留正以為不可，遂止。

translations.literal: Shuo also once proposed that bureau officers and directorate commissioners be interchangeably assigned with military officials; Drafting Attendant Liu Zheng held it impossible and it then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo once proposed rotating bureau officers and directorate commissioners with military officials; drafting attendant Liu Zheng objected and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 與右相梁克家議使事不合，克家罷去而說留，其竊政權、傾大臣類如此。

translations.literal: He discussed envoy affairs with the right chief minister Liang Kejia and disagreed; Kejia was dismissed while Shuo remained—his usurping government power and overturning great ministers were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with right chief minister Liang Kejia over embassy business; Kejia was dismissed while Shuo stayed—his habit of seizing power and toppling senior ministers followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 王抃，初為國信所小吏。

translations.literal: Wang Bian had at first been a minor clerk in the Credentials Office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bian had begun as a minor clerk in the Credentials Office.

sentences.zh: 金人求海、泗、唐、鄧、商、秦地，議久不決。

translations.literal: The Jin demanded the lands of Hai, Si, Tang, Deng, Shang, and Qin; deliberation long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin demanded Hai, Si, Tang, Deng, Shang, and Qin; debate dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 金兵至，遣抃往使，許以地，易歲貢為歲幣而還。

translations.literal: When Jin troops arrived, Bian was sent as envoy; he agreed to cede the territory, changed the annual tribute to annual payments in silk, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin armies approached, Bian was dispatched as envoy; he agreed to cede the territory, converted the annual tribute into annual payments in silk, and returned.

sentences.zh: 乾道中，積官至知閣門事，帝親信之。

translations.literal: In the Qiandao era he accumulated office to Director of the Gate, and the emperor personally trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiandao he rose to director of the Gate, and the emperor trusted him personally.

sentences.zh: 金使至，議國書禮，不合，抃以宰執虞允文命，紿其使曰：「兩朝通好自有常禮，使人何得妄生事，已牒知對境。」

translations.literal: When a Jin envoy arrived and discussion of the state-letter rites failed to agree, Bian on Chief Minister Yu Yunwen's order deceived the envoy, saying: 'The two courts' long amity has its fixed rites—how can an envoy recklessly stir up trouble? I have already notified the counterpart across the border.'
translations.idiomatic: When a Jin envoy came and talks on the state-letter rites broke down, Bian—on Chief Minister Yu Yunwen's order—bluffed the envoy: 'Amity between our courts has fixed ceremonies. How dare an envoy stir trouble? I have already notified the border counterpart.'

sentences.zh: 翌日，金使乃進書。

translations.literal: The next day the Jin envoy then presented the letter.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Jin envoy presented the letter after all.

sentences.zh: 帝以為可任，遣詣荊襄點閱軍馬。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him fit for duty and sent him to Jingxiang to inspect troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him capable and sent him to Jingxiang to review troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，兼樞密都承旨，建議以殿、步二司軍多虛籍，請各募三千人。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi era he also served as chief palace secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and proposed that the Palace and Infantry commands had many phantom rolls; he asked to recruit three thousand men for each.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi he also served as chief palace secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and argued that the Palace and Infantry commands held many ghost names on the rolls; he asked to recruit three thousand men for each.

sentences.zh: 已而殿司輒捕市人充軍，號呼滿道，軍士乘隙掠取民財。

translations.literal: Before long the Palace command abruptly seized townspeople to fill the army; shouts filled the roads and soldiers seized the chance to plunder civilians' property.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Palace command began seizing townspeople to fill the ranks; cries filled the streets and soldiers looted civilians.

sentences.zh: 帝專以罪殿前指揮使王友直，而命抃權殿前司事。

translations.literal: The emperor laid the blame solely on Palace Front commander Wang Youzhi and ordered Bian to act as Palace Front commander pro tempore.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed only Palace Front commander Wang Youzhi and put Bian in charge of the Palace Front command pro tempore.

sentences.zh: 先是，抃紿金使取國書，及使歸，金主誅之。

translations.literal: Earlier Bian had deceived the Jin envoy into taking the state letter; when the envoy returned, the Jin sovereign executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bian had tricked a Jin envoy into accepting the state letter; when that envoy returned home, the Jin ruler had him executed.

sentences.zh: 嗣歲，金使至，帝以德壽宮之命，為離席受國書，尋悔之。

translations.literal: The following year when a Jin envoy came, the emperor on the Virtuous Longevity Palace's order received the state letter standing apart from his seat; he soon regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when a Jin envoy arrived, the emperor—on orders from the Virtuous Longevity Palace—received the state letter while standing away from his seat, and soon regretted the concession.

sentences.zh: 淳熙八年，金賀正旦使至，復要帝起立如舊儀，帝遽入內，抃擅許金使用舊儀見。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chunxi, when the Jin New Year's envoy came, they again demanded that the emperor rise and stand as in the old rites; the emperor hurried into the inner quarters and Bian on his own authority permitted the Jin envoy to be received by the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chunxi the Jin New Year's envoy again demanded that the emperor rise as in the old ceremony; the emperor rushed inside, and Bian on his own authority let the Jin envoy be received under the old forms.

sentences.zh: 翌日，汝愚侍殿上，帝不懌數日。

translations.literal: The next day Yu Yongshi attended above the hall; the emperor was displeased for several days.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yu Yongshi attended in the hall; the emperor remained displeased for days.

sentences.zh: 汝愚因亟攻抃，帝遂出抃外祠，不復召。

translations.literal: Yongshi thereupon pressed his attack on Bian, and the emperor sent Bian to an outer temple post and never summoned him again.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yongshi pressed the attack on Bian, and the emperor sent Bian to an outer temple post, never to recall him.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十一年，以福州觀察使卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chunxi he died as observation commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Chunxi he died while holding the observation commissionership of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 姜特立

translations.literal: Jiang Teli
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Teli

sentences.zh: 姜特立字邦傑，麗水人。

translations.literal: Jiang Teli, style Bangjie, was a man of Lishui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Teli, courtesy name Bangjie, was a native of Lishui.

sentences.zh: 以父綬恩，補承信郎。

translations.literal: Through his father's yin privilege he was appointed Credentialed Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's yin privilege he was appointed credentialed gentleman.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，累遷福建路兵馬副都監。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi era he was repeatedly promoted to deputy overall commander of Fujian Circuit troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunxi he rose to deputy overall commander of Fujian Circuit troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 海賊姜大獠寇泉南，特立以一舟先進，擒之。

translations.literal: The sea bandit Jiang Daliao raided southern Quanzhou; Teli with one boat advanced first and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The sea bandit Jiang Daliao raided southern Quanzhou; Teli took one boat ahead of the fleet and captured him.

sentences.zh: 帥臣趙汝愚薦於朝，召見，獻所為詩百篇，除閣門舍人，命充太子宮左右春坊兼皇孫平陽王伴讀，由是得幸于太子。

translations.literal: Circuit commander Zhao Ruyu recommended him to court; summoned to audience, he presented a hundred poems he had composed and was made Gate Attendant; he was ordered to serve in the heir apparent's Eastern Palace left and right Spring Mansions and as companion reader to the imperial grandson, Prince of Pingyang—by this he won the heir apparent's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commander Zhao Ruyu recommended him at court; summoned to audience, he presented a hundred poems of his own composition and was made gate attendant, then assigned to the heir apparent's eastern palace spring mansions and as companion reader to the imperial grandson, Prince of Pingyang—thus winning the heir apparent's favor.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，除知閣門事，與譙熙載皆以春坊舊人用事，恃恩無所忌憚，時人謂曾、龍再出。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent ascended the throne, Teli was made Director of the Gate; he and Qiao Xizai both wielded power as old Eastern Palace men, relying on favor without restraint or fear—men of the time said Zeng and Long had appeared again.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent succeeded, Teli was made director of the Gate; he and Qiao Xizai, as veterans of the eastern palace, wielded power without restraint, trusting in favor—people said Zeng Di and Long Dayuan had come again.

sentences.zh: 留正為右相，執政尚闕人，特立一日語正曰：「帝以承相在位久，欲遷左揆，就二尚書中擇一人執政，孰可者？」

translations.literal: Liu Zheng was right chief minister; the administration still lacked men; one day Teli said to Zheng: 'The emperor, because the chief minister has long been in office, wishes to move him to the left seat; choosing one of the two ministers to administer—who would do?'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng was right chief minister and the council still needed men; one day Teli asked Zheng, 'The emperor, thinking you have served long as chief minister, wants to shift you to the left seat and pick one of two ministers to join the council—who would you choose?'

sentences.zh: 明日，正論其招權納賄之狀，遂奪職與外祠。

translations.literal: The next day Zheng discussed his recruiting power and taking bribes; Teli's office was then stripped and he received an outer temple post.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zheng denounced his trading in power and bribes; Teli was stripped of office and sent to an outer temple post.

sentences.zh: 帝念之，復除浙東馬步軍副總管，詔賜錢二千緡為行裝。

translations.literal: The emperor thought of him and again made him deputy overall commander of Zhe East infantry and cavalry; an edict granted two thousand strings of cash for travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor missed him and reappointed him deputy overall commander of Zhe East infantry and cavalry, with an edict granting two thousand strings of cash for travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 正引唐憲宗召吐突承璀事，乞罷相，不許。

translations.literal: Zheng cited Tang Xianzong's summoning Tu Tu Chengcui and begged to leave the chief ministership; he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng cited Tang Xianzong's recall of the eunuch Tu Tu Chengcui and asked to resign the chief ministership; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 正復言：「臣與特立勢難兩立。」

translations.literal: Zheng again said: 'I and Teli cannot stand together in power.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng added, 'Teli and I cannot share power.'

sentences.zh: 帝答曰：「成命已班，朕無反汗，卿宜自處。」

translations.literal: The emperor replied: 'The completed order has been promulgated; I will not go back on my word—you should settle matters yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, 'The appointment is already promulgated; I will not reverse myself—you must handle this on your own.'

sentences.zh: 正待罪國門外，帝不復召，而特立亦不至。

translations.literal: Zheng awaited punishment outside the National Gate; the emperor did not summon him again, and Teli also did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng waited in disgrace outside the National Gate; the emperor never recalled him, and Teli did not appear either.

sentences.zh: 甯宗受禪，特立遷和州防禦使，再奉祠，俄拜慶遠軍節度使，卒。

translations.literal: When Ningzong received the abdication, Teli was promoted to defense commissioner of Hezhou, again received a temple post, and shortly was made military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong took the throne, Teli was promoted to defense commissioner of Hezhou, received another temple post, was soon made military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army, and died.

sentences.zh: 譙熙載 附

translations.literal: Qiao Xizai—supplementary
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xizai (supplementary)

sentences.zh: 熙載亦為平陽邸伴讀，累官至忠州防禦使、知閣門事。

translations.literal: Xizai also served as companion reader at the Prince of Pingyang's residence, accumulated office to defense commissioner of Zhongzhou and Director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai too had been companion reader at the Prince of Pingyang's residence and rose to defense commissioner of Zhongzhou and director of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 紹熙中卒，較之特立頗廉勤。

translations.literal: He died in the Shaoxi era; compared with Teli he was rather honest and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Shaoxi era; beside Teli he was the more honest and diligent of the two.
